_: Per-species prompt addenda. Each value is appended to the generation prompt as a final 'Species-specific note:' paragraph for that species only. Use it when a species reliably comes out wrong and the reference photo alone doesn't fix it.
_keys: A key may be either the scientific name ('Turdus merula') or its slug ('turdus-merula'). The slug is what appears in the illustrations directory. Keys starting with an underscore are comments and are ignored.
_style: Keep a note to one or two sentences describing what to draw, not what to avoid drawing. Contrastive 'do not look like X' handling already exists for jay and swallow drift (see ANTI_REFS in pregen.py); add a note for anatomy, plumage, posture, or proportion that the model gets wrong.
_layering: An operator's own notes file is layered over this one, so a local key wins. If a note here is wrong or a local one works better, please open a PR against this file so every deployment benefits.
_regenerating: Editing a note does not by itself replace existing art. The refresh service re-renders a pose when its note changes, but only for art it generated itself - art downloaded from this repo is left alone. Locally: pass --force.
acanthis-flammea:
Common Redpoll, adult male (Acanthis flammea). NOT a rosefinch, NOT a Hoary Redpoll, NOT a Lesser Redpoll. Render the SMALLEST possible bill of a finch - tiny, dainty, fine yellow-horn cone barely longer than its width. NOT a robust seed-eater bill.

CRITICAL FACIAL FEATURES - read these very carefully (most attempts fail by inventing rosefinch features):
(1) The RED is a SMALL crimson FORECROWN PATCH only - a small triangular patch on top of the forehead just above the bill, NOT a full cap covering the whole head. Imagine a beret tipped forward. The red sits on the FOREHEAD/CROWN-FRONT only - the back-of-head and nape are plain pale brown-buff, NOT red.
(2) The BLACK is a TINY chin spot UNDER the bill - small, no larger than the eye itself, sitting at the base of the lower mandible.
(3) ABSOLUTELY NO white supercilium (eyebrow stripe). NO white line above the eye. The face is plain - pale buff with maybe a faint paler eye-ring at most.
(4) ABSOLUTELY NO dark eye-mask, NO dark eye-line through the eye, NO dark lores. The face is plain buff.
(5) ABSOLUTELY NO gray cheek patch, NO contrasting cheek panel.
(6) Tiny pale conical YELLOW-HORN bill.

PLUMAGE: pink-flushed BREAST (adult male), pink on upper breast only, fading to whitish belly. Pale STREAKY brown back and brown wings, rendered as ONE flat brown wing shape with TWO thin white strokes across it. Buff-whitish flanks with thin streaks. Notched dark brown tail. Pinkish-grey thin legs.

STRICT ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a rosefinch (Carpodacus or Uragus), NOT a House Finch. Rosefinches have an extensive red/pink hood, a thicker conical bill, and often a white supercilium - Redpolls do NOT. If you draw any white eyebrow stripe, any dark eye-mask, any gray cheek patch, any robust bill, or any red extending over the back of the head, the output is WRONG.

STYLE OVERRIDE: the wings, back, and tail MUST be 2-3 broad FLAT color zones. ABSTRACT the streaking into broad zones, not literal individual streaks. If your output has more than ~5 visible internal lines on the wing or back, IT IS WRONG.
actitis-hypoleucos: Common Sandpiper, breeding adult (Actitis hypoleucos). THE SINGLE DIAGNOSTIC MARK, without which the bird is a different sandpiper: a WHITE WEDGE OF BREAST PLUMAGE PUSHING UP IN FRONT OF THE FOLDED WING at the shoulder, separating the brown breast-side patch from the brown of the closed wing. Draw this as a clean white triangle intruding upward between two brown zones. MANDATORY: (1) UNIFORM PLAIN OLIVE-BROWN upperparts with a faint bronze sheen and NO spotting, NO spangling, NO white speckles on the back; (2) CLEAN UNMARKED WHITE underparts below a soft brown breast-side smudge - the breast band does NOT meet in the middle; (3) SHORT STRAIGHT BILL, roughly head-length, dull grey-brown with a paler base, NOT downcurved, NOT long; (4) VERY SHORT dull greenish-grey to yellow-grey legs, clearly SHORT for a wader; (5) LONG BODY held HORIZONTAL and LOW, with the TAIL PROJECTING BEYOND THE FOLDED WINGTIPS - this long-tailed, short-legged, low-slung silhouette is diagnostic; (6) a faint pale supercilium and a white eye-ring on an otherwise plain face. FLIGHT POSE: wings held BOWED AND STIFF, flickering BELOW the horizontal body line, with ONE narrow WHITE WINGBAR across each dark wing. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Spotted Sandpiper (no black breast spots, no orange bill), NOT a Wood Sandpiper (no white-spangled back, no long yellow legs, no bold supercilium), NOT a Green Sandpiper (no white rump). If the legs are long or the back is spotted, the output is WRONG.
aegithalos-caudatus: Long-tailed Tit, northern white-headed race (Aegithalos caudatus caudatus). PROPORTION IS THE WHOLE BIRD: a TINY SPHERICAL body with a NARROW BLACK TAIL AT LEAST AS LONG AGAIN AS THE BODY. If the tail is shorter than the body, the output is WRONG. MANDATORY: (1) HEAD ENTIRELY PURE WHITE - the northern race has NO black eyebrow band, NO dark head stripes, NO dark crown. The whole head and nape are clean white; (2) BODY A NEAR-PERFECT CIRCLE - no neck at all, the head merges straight into the ball of the body; (3) MINUTE BLACK BILL, stubby and triangular, smaller than the eye - the smallest bill of any bird in this set; (4) LARGE ROUND BLACK EYE set in the white head; (5) BLACK BACK AND WINGS with a PINK-WINE FLUSH on the scapulars and flanks; (6) WHITE UNDERPARTS washed pink on the belly and flanks; (7) TAIL a single narrow BLACK STROKE, graduated, with thin white edges to the outer feathers. STYLE: this bird is 4 flat zones total - white head, black-and-pink back, pink-white underside, black tail. NO feather rendering. The tail is ONE flat shape with at most one accent stroke. ANATOMY: the legs are minute and mostly hidden under belly fluff; show only tiny dark tarsi. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Bushtit, NOT a bearded reedling (no black moustache, no orange body), NOT a wagtail (the body is a ball, not a slender horizontal line).
aegolius-funereus: Boreal Owl / Tengmalm's Owl, adult (Aegolius funereus). MANDATORY: (1) NO EAR TUFTS - the head is completely round; (2) HEAD DISPROPORTIONATELY LARGE, roughly 40% of the total body bulk, sitting on a short squat body - this oversized-head look is diagnostic; (3) BROAD PALE GREY-WHITE FACIAL DISC with a DISTINCT DARK BORDER ringing its outer edge, giving a square-cornered, framed look; (4) EYES BRIGHT YELLOW, set high and close together in the disc, with BLACK BROWS ABOVE THEM that produce a permanently startled or alarmed expression - this expression is diagnostic; (5) CHOCOLATE-BROWN CROWN AND BACK covered in SMALL WHITE SPOTS, abstracted to a scatter of flat white dots, dense on the crown; (6) UNDERPARTS off-white with soft diffuse rufous-brown blotching, NOT crisp bars, NOT fine streaks; (7) PALE YELLOW-HORN BILL, small; (8) LEGS AND FEET FULLY FEATHERED WHITE, so the legs read as thick pale posts with small dark claws at the tips. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Little Owl (which has a flat brow and a scowl, not a round startled face), NOT a Tawny Owl (which has BLACK eyes and no white disc border), NOT a Northern Saw-whet Owl. If the eyes are dark, the output is WRONG. STYLE: disc is ONE flat pale zone, crown is ONE flat brown zone plus dots. ~30 strokes.
alcedo-atthis: Common Kingfisher, adult (Alcedo atthis). PROPORTION FIRST: a DUMPY, NECKLESS, LARGE-HEADED bird with a BILL AS LONG AS THE ENTIRE HEAD and a TAIL SO SHORT it is barely a stub. If the tail is more than 20% of body length, or the bill is shorter than the head, the output is WRONG. MANDATORY: (1) A BRILLIANT ELECTRIC CYAN-BLUE STRIPE running down the CENTRE OF THE BACK from nape to rump - the single brightest zone in the image; (2) CROWN AND WINGS deeper GREEN-BLUE, the crown finely spotted with pale cyan, abstracted to a few flat dots; (3) UNDERPARTS from chin-sides to vent BURNT ORANGE / RUFOUS, a large flat zone; (4) an ORANGE CHEEK PATCH behind and below the eye, with a WHITE THROAT PATCH and a WHITE NECK PATCH behind the cheek - this white-orange-white sequence on the face side is diagnostic; (5) BILL straight, heavy, DAGGER-SHAPED, black in the male; (6) LEGS EXTREMELY SHORT and CORAL RED, with tiny red feet placed far forward under the body. STYLE: exactly 4 flat zones - cyan back stripe, green-blue wings and crown, orange underside, white throat and neck patch. NO feather texture, NO iridescent gradient, NO shading. The colours are FLAT and SATURATED. ANTI-DRIFT: not any long-tailed or crested kingfisher; this bird has NO crest and NO visible tail to speak of.
anser-anser: Greylag Goose, adult (Anser anser). MANDATORY: (1) BILL LARGE, HEAVY, and UNIFORM PINK-ORANGE with a WHITE NAIL at the tip and NO black markings, NO white blaze at the base - the bill is the diagnostic feature and it is a deep triangular wedge, not a slender bill; (2) LEGS AND FEET DULL PINK; (3) HEAD AND NECK PALE GREY-BROWN, the SAME TONE as the body - the head is NOT darker than the body; (4) NECK THICK AND HEAVY with fine vertical furrows abstracted into 3-4 soft vertical strokes only; (5) BODY grey-brown with PALE FEATHER FRINGES on the flanks rendered as 2-3 broad pale bands, NOT feather-by-feather scalloping; (6) PALE ASH-GREY FOREWING PANEL contrasting with darker flight feathers - in the flight pose this pale grey forewing is diagnostic and must be visible; (7) WHITE UNDERTAIL AND VENT, and a white edge to the tail; (8) small dark eye, orange orbital skin. BULK: the body is deep-chested and heavy, the largest bird in the songbird-dominated set. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a White-fronted Goose (no white face blaze, no black belly bars), NOT a Bean Goose (no orange-and-black bill), NOT a Canada Goose (no black neck sock, no white chinstrap). If the head is black or the bill is bicoloured, the output is WRONG.
anthus-trivialis: Tree Pipit, breeding adult (Anthus trivialis). This is a PLAIN STREAKY BROWN BIRD whose identity rests on a few small marks - do not invent bold features. MANDATORY: (1) BODY SLENDER AND HORIZONTAL, wagtail-like but shorter-tailed, standing on THIN PINK LEGS; (2) UPPERPARTS warm olive-brown with soft dark streaking abstracted to 3-4 broad strokes on the mantle only; (3) BREAST WARM BUFF-YELLOW with BOLD BLACK STREAKS, and FLANKS THAT ARE NEARLY PLAIN with only fine, sparse, hair-thin streaks - the contrast between a heavily streaked breast and a nearly clean flank is THE diagnostic mark; (4) a SHORT PALE SUPERCILIUM behind the eye and a small dark spot at the rear edge of the ear-coverts; (5) BILL fine and pointed, pinkish at the base with a dark tip; (6) SHORT HIND CLAW, clearly shorter and more curved than a Meadow Pipit's - draw the hind toe short; (7) tail dark brown with white outer edges. STYLE OVERRIDE: this species invites over-rendering. The back is 2 flat zones. Breast streaks are AT MOST 6 short confident dark strokes, not stippled texture. If you draw more than 10 dark marks on the whole bird, IT IS WRONG. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Meadow Pipit (heavily streaked flanks, long hind claw), NOT a lark (no crest, no heavy bill), NOT a sparrow.
apus-apus: Common Swift, adult (Apus apus). SILHOUETTE IS THE SPECIES: a cigar-shaped body with EXTREMELY LONG, NARROW, RIGID SCYTHE-CURVED WINGS and a SHORT FORKED TAIL. MANDATORY: (1) ENTIRE BIRD UNIFORM SOOTY BLACKISH-BROWN as ONE flat zone - no pattern anywhere on the body; (2) a SMALL DULL PALE-GREY THROAT PATCH under the bill, the only pale mark on the bird and it is SMALL and INDISTINCT, not a bright white bib; (3) HEAD SMALL AND FLAT with a TINY BLACK BILL and a WIDE GAPE; (4) WINGS scythe-shaped, swept back into a stiff curve, with the outer wing NARROW AND POINTED; (5) TAIL SHORT and SHALLOWLY FORKED, no streamers; (6) FEET MINUTE and all four toes point forward - the legs are essentially invisible. PERCHED POSE OVERRIDE: swifts cannot perch on branches. Render the perched pose as the bird CLINGING VERTICALLY, body upright and pressed against an implied vertical surface, wings crossed over the back and PROJECTING WELL BEYOND THE TAIL TIP, tiny feet gripping just below the breast. Do NOT draw a horizontal songbird perch posture. FLIGHT POSE: both wings fully extended in a stiff shallow crescent, body cigar-like, tail closed to a fine point or slightly forked. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a swallow or martin (no white underparts, no rufous face, no long tail streamers, no forked deep tail), NOT a Chimney Swift. If the underparts are pale or the wings are broad, the output is WRONG.
ardea-cinerea: Grey Heron, adult (Ardea cinerea). MANDATORY: (1) HEAD AND NECK WHITE, with a BROAD BLACK STRIPE running from above the eye back over the side of the crown and trailing off the nape as TWO LONG BLACK PLUMES - these plumes must be drawn; (2) HEAVY DAGGER BILL, deep at the base, YELLOW to orange-yellow, as long as the head; (3) YELLOW EYE with a dark pupil; (4) BACK, WINGS, AND TAIL UNIFORM SOFT BLUE-GREY as one flat zone; (5) A COLUMN OF BLACK STREAKS running down the CENTRE of the white foreneck, rendered as 4-6 short confident dark dashes, and a BLACK PATCH on the shoulder at the bend of the wing; (6) LONG LOOSE GREY BREAST PLUMES hanging over the chest; (7) LEGS LONG, thick, dull yellow-brown, with long spread toes. PERCHED POSE OVERRIDE: the NECK MUST BE FOLDED INTO A TIGHT S so the head sits back ON the shoulders and the bill points forward or slightly down. Do NOT draw the neck extended vertically in the perched pose. FLIGHT POSE OVERRIDE: the NECK IS RETRACTED into a deep S with the head pulled back against the body, and THE LEGS TRAIL STRAIGHT OUT BEHIND, projecting well past the tail. A heron flying with an extended neck is WRONG - that is a crane or a stork. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Great Blue Heron (no rufous thighs, no chestnut neck), NOT a crane, NOT a stork, NOT an egret.
botaurus-stellaris: Eurasian Bittern, adult (Botaurus stellaris). MANDATORY: (1) OVERALL COLOUR WARM GOLDEN-BUFF AND TAWNY OCHRE, heavily marked with BLACK - this is a golden bird, never grey and never blue; (2) BLACK CROWN forming a solid dark cap and a BLACK MOUSTACHIAL STRIPE running down from the gape; (3) BILL heavy, dagger-shaped, DULL GREENISH-YELLOW; (4) NECK VERY THICK AND SHAGGY, much heavier than any other heron, giving a bull-necked look; (5) BODY MARKINGS abstracted into BROAD BLACK STREAKS AND BLOTCHES over 2-3 golden zones - do NOT render vermiculation or fine barring feather by feather; (6) LEGS AND FEET DISPROPORTIONATELY LARGE, pale green, with very long spreading toes; (7) EYE yellow, set low, giving a downward glare. PERCHED POSE OVERRIDE: render the classic bittern-freeze - body compressed, neck stretched UPWARD and the BILL POINTING STRAIGHT UP at the sky, so the neck streaking runs vertically. This posture is diagnostic and should be used for pose 1. FLIGHT POSE: neck partly retracted, huge feet trailing, wings broad and rounded like an owl's. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Grey Heron (never grey), NOT an American Bittern (which has a bold black neck stripe and colder brown tones). STYLE: ~30 strokes. Golden ground plus bold black marks. NO stippling.
buteo-buteo: Common Buzzard, adult intermediate morph (Buteo buteo). MANDATORY: (1) COMPACT AND BULKY with a SHORT BROAD TAIL and a SHORT THICK NECK - this is a stocky bird, not a slender one; (2) UPPERPARTS UNIFORM DARK EARTH-BROWN as one flat zone; (3) UNDERPARTS pale cream with a DARK BROWN BREAST BAND ACROSS THE UPPER CHEST and a PALE CRESCENT-SHAPED BAND ACROSS THE LOWER BREAST - this pale U-shaped chest crescent is the diagnostic mark and must be drawn as a clean flat pale band; (4) DARK BROWN FLANKS AND THIGHS framing the pale belly; (5) BILL SHORT, deeply HOOKED, dark grey with a YELLOW CERE at the base; (6) EYE DARK BROWN, not yellow, not orange; (7) LEGS AND FEET YELLOW, short and thick, with heavy black talons; (8) TAIL brown, finely barred, with ONE broader dark subterminal band - abstract to at most 3 bands total. FLIGHT POSE OVERRIDE: wings BROAD AND ROUNDED with fingered primaries, held in a shallow V, tail SPREAD INTO A WIDE FAN. Show pale panels at the base of the primaries on the underwing and a dark carpal comma at the bend of each wing. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a falcon (wings are broad and rounded, never pointed), NOT a Red-tailed Hawk (no rufous tail), NOT a goshawk (no white supercilium, no long tail), NOT an eagle. If the eye is yellow or the wings are pointed, the output is WRONG.
calcarius-lapponicus: Lapland Longspur / Lapland Bunting, BREEDING ADULT MALE (Calcarius lapponicus). RENDER BREEDING PLUMAGE ONLY - the winter bird is a plain streaky brown bunting and is WRONG for this set. MANDATORY: (1) FACE, THROAT, AND UPPER BREAST SOLID JET BLACK, forming a hood over the front of the head and down onto the chest; (2) A BROAD CREAM-WHITE STRIPE starting behind the eye and CURVING DOWN AND FORWARD around the black cheek to the side of the breast - this hooked white band separating black face from black breast is THE diagnostic mark; (3) A LARGE BRIGHT CHESTNUT-RUFOUS PANEL COVERING THE NAPE AND HINDNECK, a clean flat orange-brown zone directly behind the black head; (4) BILL SHORT, CONICAL, BRIGHT YELLOW with a dark tip; (5) BACK streaked black and buff, abstracted to 3 broad zones; (6) UNDERPARTS below the black breast WHITE with a few dark flank streaks only; (7) BODY LONG AND LOW, held horizontally close to the ground on SHORT DARK LEGS with a NOTABLY LONG STRAIGHT HIND CLAW - draw the hind claw as a long straight spike; (8) tail dark with white outer feathers. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Reed Bunting (which has a white MOUSTACHE and full white collar, no chestnut nape, and a dark bill), NOT a Snow Bunting (no large white wing panels), NOT a House Sparrow.
carduelis-carduelis: European Goldfinch, adult (Carduelis carduelis). MANDATORY, and the face pattern must be exact: (1) A BRIGHT CRIMSON-RED FACE MASK surrounding the base of the bill and extending BACK PAST THE EYE, bordered behind by a CLEAN WHITE CHEEK, and above by a BLACK CROWN THAT WRAPS DOWN THE SIDE OF THE NECK as a black band - the red-white-black sequence on the head is the whole species; (2) BILL LONG, SHARPLY POINTED, CONICAL, IVORY-PINK WITH A DARK TIP - noticeably more pointed and slender than a typical finch bill; (3) BACK AND FLANKS WARM MILKY BROWN, breast sides brown, belly and vent WHITE; (4) WING SOLID BLACK crossed by ONE BROAD FLAT GOLDEN-YELLOW BAND running the full length of the folded wing, with small WHITE SPOTS at the very tips of the black primaries; (5) TAIL BLACK with small white spots near the tip; (6) LEGS pale pinkish-brown. FLIGHT POSE: the broad yellow wingbar must blaze across BOTH spread wings as a single bold flat band, and the RUMP IS WHITE. STYLE: the wing is ONE flat black shape with ONE flat yellow band - not a feather diagram. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT an American Goldfinch (which is all-yellow with a black cap and no red face), NOT a siskin (no red face, no white cheek), NOT a linnet. If the face lacks red or the wing lacks a solid yellow band, the output is WRONG.
certhia-familiaris: Eurasian Treecreeper, adult (Certhia familiaris). POSTURE IS THE SPECIES. Render BOTH poses with the bird PRESSED VERTICALLY AGAINST AN IMPLIED TRUNK, HEAD UP, body angled steeply, with the STIFF POINTED TAIL BRACED DOWNWARD BEHIND THE BODY as a prop. Do NOT draw a horizontal songbird perch posture. MANDATORY: (1) BILL FINE, LONG, and SMOOTHLY DOWNCURVED like a thin sickle, roughly head-length - this bill is diagnostic and must not be short or straight; (2) UPPERPARTS mottled brown, buff, and cream, abstracted into 2-3 flat zones with a scatter of small pale dashes, never feather-by-feather; (3) UNDERPARTS SILKY WHITE, clean and unmarked from chin to vent, contrasting hard with the brown back; (4) a distinct WHITE SUPERCILIUM above a dark eye-line; (5) TAIL long, pointed, warm brown, with STIFF POINTED FEATHER TIPS; (6) LEGS pale brown with LONG CURVED CLAWS, both feet gripping the implied bark on the SAME vertical plane, one slightly higher than the other. FLIGHT POSE: undulating, showing a pale buff band across the spread wings. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a nuthatch (which is blue-grey above, goes head-DOWN, has a straight chisel bill and a short tail), NOT a wren (which has a cocked short tail and a straight bill). If the bill is straight or the bird is head-down, the output is WRONG.
chloris-chloris: European Greenfinch, adult male (Chloris chloris). MANDATORY: (1) BULKY AND THICK-NECKED with a LARGE HEAD and NO visible neck - a heavy-built finch, not a slim one; (2) BILL VERY LARGE, DEEP, CONICAL, and PALE IVORY-PINK - the depth of the bill at its base is nearly the depth of the head; (3) BODY UNIFORM OLIVE-GREEN, brighter yellow-green on the breast and rump, greyer on the cheek and the side of the neck; (4) A BOLD FLAT LEMON-YELLOW PANEL ALONG THE LEADING EDGE OF THE FOLDED WING, forming a bright yellow stripe against grey primaries - this yellow wing flash is diagnostic; (5) BRIGHT YELLOW PATCHES AT THE BASE OF THE OUTER TAIL FEATHERS on each side of a dark forked tail - these yellow tail flashes must be visible in both poses; (6) LEGS pale pink, short and sturdy; (7) EYE dark, small, with plain unmarked lores. FLIGHT POSE: both spread wings show the broad yellow leading-edge flash and the fanned tail shows yellow at the sides of a dark centre. STYLE: 3 flat zones - green body, grey-and-yellow wing, dark tail with yellow sides. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a siskin (no black cap, no streaking, much bulkier), NOT a female House Sparrow, NOT a warbler (the bill is massive).
cinclus-cinclus: White-throated Dipper, adult (Cinclus cinclus). MANDATORY: (1) BODY SHORT, ROUND, AND POWERFULLY BUILT with a VERY SHORT TAIL COCKED UPWARD - a wren-shaped bird scaled up to thrush size; (2) HEAD AND NAPE WARM CHOCOLATE-BROWN, contrasting with a DARKER SLATE-BLACK BACK, WINGS, AND TAIL; (3) A LARGE CLEAN WHITE BIB covering the chin, throat, and upper breast, cut off SHARPLY at the bottom edge; (4) DIRECTLY BELOW THE WHITE BIB a BROAD CHESTNUT-RUFOUS BAND across the breast, which then blends into the dark belly - the white-then-chestnut-then-dark sequence down the front is THE diagnostic mark and must be three clean flat bands; (5) BILL short, straight, slender, and BLACK; (6) LEGS STOUT and PALE GREY-PINK, set well forward, with strong toes; (7) a white upper eyelid that flashes when blinking - render the eye as a small dark dot with a fine pale arc above it. POSTURE: upright, chest thrust forward, tail cocked, standing on an implied rock. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a wren (far larger, white bib), NOT a thrush (tail far too short), NOT an American Dipper (which is uniformly grey with NO white bib). If the throat is not white, the output is WRONG.
coccothraustes-coccothraustes: Hawfinch, adult male (Coccothraustes coccothraustes). THE BILL IS THE BIRD: an ENORMOUS conical bill, so deep at the base that it is nearly as tall as the head and takes up a third of the head's profile. If the bill looks like a normal finch bill, the output is WRONG. MANDATORY: (1) BILL MASSIVE, triangular, STEEL BLUE-GREY in breeding condition, meeting the forehead with almost no break; (2) HEAD LARGE and WARM ORANGE-BROWN, with a GREY NAPE COLLAR wrapping around the back of the neck; (3) A BLACK MASK around the base of the bill and a SMALL BLACK BIB on the chin; (4) BODY TOP-HEAVY - huge head and chest tapering to a SHORT TAIL, with a THICK BULL NECK; (5) BACK dark chestnut-brown, UNDERPARTS pinkish-buff; (6) WING BLACK with a BROAD WHITE BAND across the coverts, forming a bold flat white block; (7) TAIL SHORT with a WHITE TIP; (8) LEGS pink, short and thick. FLIGHT POSE: the spread wings show LARGE WHITE PANELS across the middle of each wing and the white-tipped short tail is obvious. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Bullfinch (no black cap, no rose breast), NOT a grosbeak of the Americas, NOT a crossbill. STYLE: 4 flat zones and a black-and-white wing block. ~30 strokes.
columba-livia: Rock Dove / Feral Pigeon, wild-type adult (Columba livia). Render the WILD blue-grey type only, not a white or pied feral variant. MANDATORY: (1) BODY CLEAN BLUE-GREY, paler on the back and wings, with a DARKER GREY HEAD; (2) TWO BOLD BLACK BARS ACROSS THE FOLDED WING, well separated, running as clean flat black stripes across the pale grey wing - these two bars are diagnostic and must both be drawn; (3) A GLOSSY GREEN-AND-PURPLE IRIDESCENT PATCH on the side of the neck, rendered as one flat zone of shifting green-violet, not as gradient shading; (4) WHITE RUMP visible between the grey back and the dark tail band - important in the flight pose; (5) TAIL grey with a BROAD BLACK TERMINAL BAND; (6) BILL dark grey with a PROMINENT WHITE FLESHY CERE at the base; (7) EYE ORANGE-RED; (8) LEGS AND FEET PINK-RED, short. PROPORTION: small rounded head, deep chest, medium tail. FLIGHT POSE: wings pointed and angled, white rump and black tail band both clearly visible. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Wood Pigeon (no white neck patch, no white wing slash, much smaller and neater), NOT a Collared Dove (no black neck ring, not sandy), NOT a Stock Dove (which lacks both the white rump and the bold wing bars).
columba-palumbus: Common Wood Pigeon, adult (Columba palumbus). MANDATORY: (1) LARGE AND HEAVY, deep-chested, with a SMALL HEAD on a THICK NECK - noticeably bulkier than a Rock Dove; (2) A LARGE CLEAN WHITE PATCH ON THE SIDE OF THE NECK, bordered below and behind by a narrow band of GREEN-PURPLE IRIDESCENCE - this white neck patch is the diagnostic mark and must be a bold flat white oval, present in BOTH poses; (3) A BROAD WHITE SLASH ACROSS THE WING, forming a crescent along the leading edge of the folded wing and, in flight, a BOLD WHITE CRESCENT BAND across each spread wing; (4) HEAD AND UPPERPARTS SOFT BLUE-GREY, BREAST WARM VINOUS PINK, belly pale grey; (5) BILL ORANGE-PINK with a YELLOW TIP and a WHITE CERE; (6) EYE PALE LEMON-YELLOW, not orange, not red; (7) TAIL long, grey, with a BROAD BLACK TERMINAL BAND; (8) LEGS deep pink-red. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Rock Dove (which has two black wing bars, a white rump, an orange eye and no neck patch), NOT a Collared Dove (which is sandy with a thin black hind-neck ring). If the neck lacks a white patch or the wing lacks a white slash, the output is WRONG.
corvus-corax: Common Raven, adult (Corvus corax). SCALE AND SHAPE ARE THE SPECIES - it must not look like a crow. MANDATORY: (1) BILL MASSIVE, DEEP, and slightly ARCHED along the culmen, with a CURVED TIP and a covering of stiff BRISTLES over the top third of the bill from the base - draw those nasal bristles as a few confident strokes; (2) A SHAGGY THROAT of loose pointed feathers hanging below the chin as a spiky beard - this hackle is diagnostic and must be visible in the perched pose; (3) HEAD LARGE AND FLAT-CROWNED with a heavy brow; (4) TAIL LONG AND WEDGE-SHAPED, tapering to a central point - in the flight pose the tail MUST be a clear diamond or wedge, never fan-shaped and never square; (5) ENTIRE BIRD BLACK, rendered as TWO flat zones - a base black and a slightly blue-purple sheen zone across the back and wing - with no more sheen than that; (6) WINGS LONG with long fingered primaries; (7) LEGS AND FEET heavy, black, scaly. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Hooded Crow (no grey anywhere), NOT a Carrion Crow or American Crow (bill far heavier, throat shaggy, tail wedge-shaped rather than square), NOT a rook (no bare pale face patch, keep the bill base feathered). STYLE: flat black zones. NO feather-by-feather rendering on black.
corvus-cornix: Hooded Crow, adult (Corvus cornix). THE BIRD IS TWO-TONE AND THE BOUNDARY MUST BE SHARP. MANDATORY: (1) HEAD, THROAT, BIB, WINGS, AND TAIL SOLID GLOSSY BLACK; (2) MANTLE, BACK, RUMP, BREAST, BELLY, AND FLANKS UNIFORM ASH-GREY - a clean, flat, mid grey with no mottling and no brown; (3) THE BLACK BIB ENDS IN A CLEAN CURVED EDGE ACROSS THE UPPER BREAST, and the black of the head does not creep down over the grey mantle - render the grey-to-black transitions as HARD FLAT EDGES, never as blended gradients; (4) BILL STOUT, BLACK, straight-culmened with a modest hook, feathered at the base; (5) EYE dark; (6) TAIL medium length and SQUARE-TIPPED, never wedge-shaped; (7) LEGS AND FEET black and sturdy. FLIGHT POSE: the grey body and black wings must read as a bold two-tone shape from any angle, and the tail is square. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Raven (square tail, no shaggy throat, smaller bill), NOT a Carrion Crow (which is entirely black), NOT a Jackdaw (no pale eye, no grey nape shawl). If the body is all black or the grey is smudged into the black, the output is WRONG.
cuculus-canorus: Common Cuckoo, adult male grey morph (Cuculus canorus). This species is routinely mistaken for a hawk - the details below prevent that. MANDATORY: (1) HEAD, THROAT, BREAST, AND UPPERPARTS UNIFORM SOFT BLUE-GREY as one flat zone; (2) BELLY WHITE with FINE DARK HORIZONTAL BARRING, abstracted to 4-6 clean thin flat bars, never dense stippling; (3) BILL SLENDER, slightly downcurved at the tip, DARK GREY WITH A YELLOW GAPE AND BASE - a small soft bill, NOT a raptor's hooked beak; (4) EYE and EYE-RING BRIGHT YELLOW-ORANGE, with a small dark pupil; (5) FEET YELLOW and ZYGODACTYL - two toes forward, two toes back; draw the foot with a clear front-and-back split; (6) BODY LONG AND SLENDER with a LONG GRADUATED TAIL that has WHITE SPOTS ALONG THE EDGES and a white tip; (7) WINGS POINTED and, in the perched pose, DROOPED BELOW THE TAIL LINE while the tail is often slightly raised - this drooped-wing, cocked-tail posture is diagnostic. FLIGHT POSE: wings pointed and beaten BELOW THE BODY LINE, never raised above the back, head slightly raised, long tail trailing. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Sparrowhawk (no hooked bill, no talons, no broad rounded wings), NOT a falcon, NOT a dove. If you draw a hooked raptor bill or gripping talons, the output is WRONG.
cyanistes-caeruleus: Eurasian Blue Tit, adult (Cyanistes caeruleus). The face pattern is the species and it is precise. MANDATORY: (1) A BRIGHT COBALT-BLUE CAP on the top of the head, ENCIRCLED BY A THIN WHITE BAND that runs across the forehead, above the eye, and around the back of the nape - the blue cap sits inside a white ring like a skullcap; (2) A NARROW DARK BLUE-BLACK LINE RUNNING THROUGH THE EYE from the bill to the nape, crossing an otherwise WHITE CHEEK; (3) A SMALL DARK BLUE CHIN PATCH under the bill, joining a thin dark collar around the throat; (4) UNDERPARTS BRIGHT LEMON-YELLOW with a FAINT NARROW DARK LINE running down the centre of the belly; (5) BACK YELLOW-GREEN; (6) WINGS AND TAIL COBALT BLUE, the wing crossed by ONE THIN WHITE BAR; (7) BILL VERY SHORT, black, conical; (8) LEGS blue-grey, thin. PROPORTION: tiny, round, large-headed, short-tailed. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Great Tit (no black head, no black belly stripe, no white cheek oval on a black hood), NOT an Azure Tit, NOT a chickadee. If the crown is not blue or the eye-line is missing, the output is WRONG.
cygnus-olor: Mute Swan, adult (Cygnus olor). MANDATORY: (1) BILL ORANGE with a BLACK BASE AND BLACK NOSTRIL AREA, and a PROMINENT BLACK KNOB / CARUNCLE swelling at the top of the bill base where it meets the forehead - this black knob is THE diagnostic mark and must be clearly drawn; (2) A BLACK MASK from the bill base through the eye, so the eye sits inside a small black patch; (3) NECK LONG and held in a GRACEFUL S-CURVE with the bill angled DOWNWARD, not straight up; (4) PLUMAGE PURE WHITE throughout, rendered as ONE flat white zone with at most two soft grey accent strokes for the wing edge; (5) WINGS ARCHED SLIGHTLY OVER THE BACK in the perched pose, with the innermost feathers raised into a soft hump; (6) LEGS AND WEBBED FEET BLACK; (7) TAIL SHORT AND POINTED, held clear of the water line. FLIGHT POSE: neck fully extended straight forward, wings very long and broad, feet tucked back under the tail. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Whooper Swan or Bewick's Swan (which have YELLOW-AND-BLACK bills, NO knob, and hold the neck straight and stiff), NOT a goose. If there is no black knob or the bill is yellow, the output is WRONG.
delichon-urbicum: Common House Martin, adult (Delichon urbicum). MANDATORY: (1) A LARGE, CLEAN, SQUARE WHITE RUMP PATCH between the blue-black back and the dark tail - this white rump is THE diagnostic mark and must be a bold flat white block visible in BOTH poses; (2) UPPERPARTS GLOSSY BLUE-BLACK, including the crown right down to below the eye; (3) UNDERPARTS ENTIRELY PURE WHITE from the CHIN downward - the throat is WHITE, with no red, no chestnut, and no breast band of any kind; (4) TAIL SHORT AND SHALLOWLY FORKED, with NO streamers and no elongated outer feathers; (5) WINGS broad-based and triangular, shorter and blunter than a swallow's; (6) LEGS AND FEET COVERED IN WHITE FEATHERING right down to the toes - draw the tiny legs as white tufts; (7) BILL minute and black, eye small and dark. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Barn Swallow (which has a RED throat, a dark breast band, and long tail streamers), NOT a Sand Martin (which is plain SANDY BROWN above with a BROWN BREAST BAND and no white rump), NOT a Tree Swallow. If the throat is not white, if the tail has streamers, or if the rump is dark, the output is WRONG.
dendrocopos-major: Great Spotted Woodpecker, adult MALE (Dendrocopos major). MANDATORY: (1) TWO LARGE OVAL WHITE SHOULDER PATCHES, one on each scapular, forming bold white ovals against a solid BLACK BACK - the back between them is BLACK with NO white stripe down the centre; (2) FACE WHITE, crossed by a BLACK MOUSTACHIAL STRIPE that runs from the bill down and BACK to join the BLACK NAPE and a black collar - this connected black bridle framing a white cheek is diagnostic; (3) A SMALL BRIGHT RED PATCH ON THE NAPE at the back of the head only, in the male; the crown itself is BLACK; (4) VENT AND UNDERTAIL BRIGHT CRIMSON, contrasting with clean off-WHITE UNDERPARTS that are otherwise unmarked - no streaks, no bars, no spots on the breast; (5) WINGS BLACK with ROWS OF WHITE SPOTS forming clean bars across the flight feathers, abstracted to 3-4 rows of flat white dots; (6) BILL a straight grey CHISEL, stout; (7) LEGS grey, zygodactyl. POSE 1 OVERRIDE: vertical, clinging head-up against an implied trunk with the STIFF TAIL BRACED DOWNWARD as a third support. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Hairy or Downy Woodpecker (no white back stripe, no white face stripes), NOT an Acorn Woodpecker (dark eye, not white). If the crown is red or the back has a white stripe, the output is WRONG.
dryocopus-martius: Black Woodpecker, adult male (Dryocopus martius). MANDATORY: (1) ENTIRE BODY MATT SOOTY BLACK, one flat zone, with no white anywhere - no wing bars, no back stripe, no white spots; (2) A BRIGHT CRIMSON CROWN COVERING THE WHOLE TOP OF THE HEAD from forehead to nape in the male, forming a clean red cap on flat black; (3) BILL LONG, STRAIGHT, and PALE IVORY-YELLOW with a dark tip, chisel-ended, noticeably long relative to the head; (4) EYE PALE WHITE-YELLOW with a small dark pupil, staring out of the black head - this pale eye against black is diagnostic; (5) BODY LONG, LEAN, and RANGY with a SNAKY NECK - crow-sized, not compact; (6) TAIL long, stiff, and POINTED, braced downward in the perched pose; (7) LEGS grey, zygodactyl, with strong claws. POSE 1: vertical on an implied trunk, head up, neck slightly extended, tail pressed down. FLIGHT POSE: wings broad and rounded, flight looks heavy and irregular; body remains uniformly black with a red crown. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Pileated Woodpecker (which has a pointed crest, white face stripes, and white underwings), NOT a crow (chisel bill, pale eye, zygodactyl feet). If the bird has a crest or any white, the output is WRONG.
emberiza-citrinella: Yellowhammer, breeding adult male (Emberiza citrinella). MANDATORY: (1) HEAD ALMOST ENTIRELY BRIGHT LEMON-YELLOW - forehead, crown, face, and throat - with only faint olive smudging on the crown sides and behind the eye; the yellow head is the single strongest zone in the image; (2) UNDERPARTS YELLOW, warming to a RUFOUS-CHESTNUT WASH across the breast sides and flanks with a few fine dark streaks; (3) A BRIGHT CHESTNUT-RUFOUS RUMP, unstreaked, which is diagnostic and must be visible in the flight pose; (4) BACK warm brown with bold dark streaks abstracted to 3-4 broad strokes; (5) BILL SMALL, CONICAL, BLUE-GREY, with the lower mandible paler; (6) TAIL LONG and NOTCHED with WHITE OUTER FEATHERS that flash in flight; (7) LEGS pinkish-brown, slim. SHAPE: a long-bodied, long-tailed bunting, slimmer and longer-tailed than a finch. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Reed Bunting (no black hood, no white collar), NOT a canary or serin (the head is not uniformly clean yellow, the body is streaked brown), NOT a Cirl Bunting (no black eye-stripe or black throat band). If the rump is grey or the head lacks yellow, the output is WRONG.
emberiza-schoeniclus: Reed Bunting, BREEDING ADULT MALE (Emberiza schoeniclus). Render breeding plumage only. MANDATORY: (1) HEAD AND THROAT SOLID BLACK, forming a hood over the crown, face, chin, and central throat; (2) A BROAD WHITE MOUSTACHIAL STRIPE running from the base of the bill DOWN AND BACK along the lower edge of the black cheek, connecting to a CLEAN WHITE COLLAR that wraps around the back of the neck - this white moustache curving into a white collar is THE diagnostic mark; (3) BACK rich brown with BOLD BLACK STREAKS, abstracted to 3 broad zones with a few dark strokes; (4) UNDERPARTS below the black bib WHITE with fine dark streaks on the flanks only; (5) BILL SMALL, CONICAL, DARK GREY-BLACK - not yellow; (6) TAIL fairly long, notched, with WHITE OUTER TAIL FEATHERS; (7) LEGS dark brown, slim; (8) the crown often looks slightly peaked or ruffled. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Lapland Longspur (which has a CHESTNUT NAPE, a yellow bill, and a hooked cream face-band rather than a white collar), NOT a House Sparrow (no grey crown, no chestnut nape), NOT a Yellowhammer. If the nape is chestnut or the bill is yellow, the output is WRONG.
erithacus-rubecula: European Robin, adult (Erithacus rubecula). MANDATORY, and the extent of the orange is the key point: (1) A LARGE ORANGE-RED ZONE COVERING THE FOREHEAD, THE FACE AROUND AND BELOW THE EYE, THE CHIN, THE THROAT, AND THE UPPER BREAST as one continuous flat shape - the orange reaches UP OVER THE FOREHEAD to the bill and SURROUNDS THE EYE; it is not a bib confined to the chest; (2) A SOFT BLUE-GREY BORDER separating the orange from the brown crown and from the pale belly, running down the side of the neck and around the breast edge; (3) UPPERPARTS PLAIN WARM OLIVE-BROWN with no streaking, no wingbars, no markings of any kind; (4) BELLY AND VENT off-white, flanks buff; (5) EYE LARGE, ROUND, and BLACK, prominent in the orange face, with no eye-ring, no supercilium, no eye-line; (6) BILL SHORT, fine, and dark; (7) LEGS THIN and dark brown; (8) BODY ROUND AND PLUMP with an upright posture and a short tail. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT an American Robin (which is a large thrush with a grey back, a dark head, and a yellow bill), NOT a Bluethroat, NOT a redstart. If the orange stops below the chin or the back is grey, the output is WRONG.
falco-tinnunculus: Common Kestrel, adult MALE (Falco tinnunculus). MANDATORY: (1) HEAD BLUE-GREY, including the crown and nape, with a NARROW DARK MOUSTACHIAL STRIPE dropping from below the eye - a thin dark line, not a broad helmet; (2) BACK AND WING COVERTS WARM CHESTNUT-RUFOUS, marked with SMALL BLACK DIAMOND SPOTS, abstracted to a scatter of 6-8 flat dark marks - not dense speckling; (3) TAIL BLUE-GREY with ONE BROAD BLACK SUBTERMINAL BAND and a NARROW WHITE TIP; this single bold black tail band is diagnostic; (4) UNDERPARTS warm buff with fine dark streaks and spots, at most 8 marks total; (5) BILL SHORT and HOOKED with a TOOTHED upper mandible, dark tip, with a YELLOW CERE at the base; (6) EYE LARGE and DARK BROWN with a YELLOW ORBITAL RING; (7) LEGS AND FEET BRIGHT YELLOW with black talons; (8) WINGS LONG AND POINTED, and in the perched pose the wingtips fall SHORT of the tail tip. FLIGHT POSE: wings narrow and sharply pointed, tail fanned showing the black band. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Peregrine (no broad black helmet, no barred underparts), NOT a Sparrowhawk or buzzard (wings must be pointed, never rounded), NOT a Merlin. If the wings are rounded or the tail lacks a broad black band, the output is WRONG.
ficedula-hypoleuca: European Pied Flycatcher, breeding adult MALE (Ficedula hypoleuca). MANDATORY: (1) UPPERPARTS SOLID BLACK - crown, nape, back, wings, and tail as one flat black zone; (2) UNDERPARTS PURE WHITE from chin to vent, clean and unmarked, meeting the black in a HARD FLAT EDGE at the side of the neck and breast; (3) A SMALL CLEAN WHITE PATCH ON THE FOREHEAD just above the bill - one or two white spots, small but sharp; (4) A BOLD WHITE PANEL ON THE FOLDED WING, a large flat white block on the inner flight feathers, plus a thin white edge along the tertials - this white wing block is diagnostic and must be one solid shape, not a row of bars; (5) WHITE ON THE OUTER TAIL FEATHERS, visible as white edges on the dark tail; (6) BILL SHORT, BROAD-BASED, and FLAT, black, with a wide gape for catching insects; (7) HEAD LARGE and rounded, BODY COMPACT, TAIL SHORT; (8) LEGS very short and black. POSTURE: upright, alert, head-on, often with the tail flicked. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Collared Flycatcher (which has a broad WHITE NECK COLLAR and a white rump), NOT a Red-breasted Flycatcher (no orange throat), NOT a chickadee. If a white collar wraps the neck, the output is WRONG.
ficedula-parva: Red-breasted Flycatcher, adult male (Ficedula parva). MANDATORY: (1) A SMALL ORANGE-RED THROAT PATCH covering only the chin and throat, bordered by GREY on the sides of the head and neck - the orange is CONFINED to the throat and does NOT extend down over the breast or belly; (2) THE REST OF THE UNDERPARTS OFF-WHITE, clean and unmarked; (3) UPPERPARTS PLAIN WARM GREY-BROWN with no streaking and no wingbars; (4) A CONSPICUOUS WHITE EYE-RING on a plain face, with a large dark eye - the eye looks big for the head; (5) TAIL BLACK with LARGE WHITE PATCHES AT THE BASE OF THE OUTER TAIL FEATHERS, forming white panels on either side of a black tail - this black tail with white sides is diagnostic and must be drawn in BOTH poses; (6) THE TAIL IS FREQUENTLY COCKED UPWARD in the perched pose - draw it raised above the body line; (7) BILL small, dark, broad at the base; (8) LEGS short and black; (9) VERY SMALL - the smallest flycatcher shape, round-headed and compact. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a European Robin (the orange is throat-only, the back is grey-brown, the tail is black-and-white), NOT a Pied Flycatcher (no black-and-white plumage). If the orange spreads onto the breast or the tail lacks white bases, the output is WRONG.
fringilla-coelebs: Common Chaffinch, breeding adult MALE (Fringilla coelebs). MANDATORY: (1) CROWN AND NAPE SLATE BLUE-GREY, forming a clean grey cap and hindneck; (2) FACE, THROAT, AND BREAST WARM PINK-BRICK, extending down onto the flanks; (3) BACK WARM CHESTNUT-BROWN and RUMP OLIVE-GREEN; (4) THE WING PATTERN IS THE SPECIES - a BOLD WHITE SHOULDER BLOCK on the lesser coverts, a SECOND CLEAN WHITE BAR across the greater coverts below it, and YELLOW-WHITE EDGES to the black flight feathers; draw the wing as ONE flat dark shape carrying TWO bold white marks, the upper one a block and the lower one a bar; (5) TAIL DARK with WHITE OUTER TAIL FEATHERS flashing at the sides; (6) BILL CONICAL and BLUE-GREY in breeding condition, with a dark tip; (7) LEGS pinkish-brown; (8) a small dark forehead band above the bill. FLIGHT POSE: the double white wing marks and white outer tail feathers must both be obvious. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Brambling (no orange shoulder, no white rump, no black head), NOT a bullfinch (no black cap), NOT a House Sparrow. If the wing lacks the white shoulder block, the output is WRONG.
gallinago-media: Great Snipe, adult (Gallinago media). MANDATORY: (1) BILL LONG, STRAIGHT, and STOUT, roughly 1.5 to 2 times the head length, dull grey-brown, with a blunt flexible tip - long but PROPORTIONALLY SHORTER AND THICKER than a Common Snipe's; (2) BODY BULKY, HEAVY-BELLIED, and thickset, standing LOW on SHORT greenish-grey LEGS; (3) HEAD PATTERN: a PALE CREAM MEDIAN CROWN STRIPE running front to back down the centre of a dark crown, with a pale supercilium and a dark eye-stripe below it; (4) UPPERPARTS a mosaic of black, chestnut, and buff, with FOUR LONG PALE BUFF STRIPES running lengthwise down the back - abstract these into four clean flat pale bands over a dark ground, never feather-by-feather; (5) FLANKS AND BELLY HEAVILY BARRED with dark chevrons, abstracted to 4-6 clean flat bars, and the barring EXTENDS RIGHT ACROSS THE BELLY; (6) BOLD WHITE OUTER TAIL CORNERS, drawn as clean white wedges on each side of the tail - diagnostic and must be visible; (7) WING COVERTS showing white tips forming pale bars. FLIGHT POSE: heavy, direct, low, with the bill angled DOWN and the tail showing white corners. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Common Snipe (which has a longer thinner bill, a white belly, and no white tail corners), NOT a Woodcock (which is bigger-eyed with transverse crown bars). STYLE: max ~30 strokes, broad flat zones, no stippling.
garrulus-glandarius: Eurasian Jay, adult (Garrulus glandarius). THE BODY IS PINK-BROWN, NOT BLUE. Only a small wing panel is blue. MANDATORY: (1) BODY, BACK, BREAST, AND BELLY WARM PINKISH-BUFF, a soft flat wine-brown, over the whole bird; (2) CROWN WHITISH with FINE BLACK STREAKS, abstracted to a few short dark strokes, and often raised into a low ragged crest; (3) A BROAD BLACK MOUSTACHIAL STRIPE dropping from the bill down the side of the WHITE THROAT - a thick black wedge, diagnostic; (4) A SMALL PANEL OF SKY-BLUE BARRED WITH FINE BLACK LINES at the bend of the wing only - draw 4-6 clean black bars across a small blue block, and put blue NOWHERE ELSE on the bird; (5) WINGS otherwise BLACK with a WHITE PANEL on the inner flight feathers; (6) RUMP PURE WHITE contrasting with a SOLID BLACK TAIL - this white rump against black tail must be visible in the flight pose; (7) EYE PALE BLUE-WHITE with a dark pupil; (8) BILL BLACK, stout; LEGS pinkish-brown. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Blue Jay (no blue crest, no blue back, no black necklace, no white face), NOT a magpie. If the body or head is blue, the output is WRONG.
gavia-stellata: Red-throated Loon / Red-throated Diver, BREEDING ADULT (Gavia stellata). Render breeding plumage only. MANDATORY: (1) A DEEP RUST-RED TRIANGULAR PATCH covering the FRONT AND SIDES OF THE THROAT, tapering to a point at the base of the neck - this is the only bright colour on the bird; (2) HEAD AND SIDES OF NECK PLAIN SOFT DOVE-GREY, unmarked; (3) THE BACK OF THE NECK AND HINDNECK finely striped BLACK AND WHITE in narrow vertical lines - abstract to 5-7 clean thin strokes; (4) BACK, WINGS, AND UPPERPARTS PLAIN DARK GREY-BROWN with NO white spots, NO checkerboard, NO chequered panels of any kind; (5) UNDERPARTS WHITE; (6) BILL SLENDER, THIN, and DAGGER-LIKE, and HELD ANGLED SLIGHTLY UPWARD - the uptilted thin bill is diagnostic; (7) EYE DARK RED; (8) BODY LOW, LONG, and STREAMLINED, sitting deep with legs set far back at the rear of the body. FLIGHT POSE: hunchbacked profile with the neck drooping slightly BELOW the body line, feet trailing behind, wings narrow and pointed. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Black-throated or Great Northern Diver (no black-and-white chequered back, no black throat), NOT a grebe, NOT a cormorant. If the back is chequered or the throat is black, the output is WRONG.
grus-grus: Common Crane, adult (Grus grus). MANDATORY: (1) A BOLD WHITE STRIPE starting behind the eye and running DOWN THE BACK AND SIDE OF THE NECK, separating the BLACK FOREneck and face from the grey body - this white neck stripe is diagnostic; (2) FACE, FORECROWN, CHIN, THROAT, AND FORENECK BLACK; (3) A SMALL BARE RED PATCH ON THE REAR CROWN, drawn as a modest red cap on the back of the head only, not a full red head; (4) BODY UNIFORM ASH-GREY as one flat zone; (5) A DROOPING BUSTLE OF LOOSE, SHAGGY, DARK-TIPPED PLUMES over the rear end, hanging past the short tail like a feathered skirt - this bustle must be drawn and is a key silhouette cue; (6) BILL STRAIGHT, dull horn-grey, roughly head-length, NOT a dagger and NOT downcurved; (7) LEGS VERY LONG and BLACK-GREY; (8) NECK LONG and held STRAIGHT. FLIGHT POSE OVERRIDE: unlike a heron, the CRANE FLIES WITH THE NECK FULLY EXTENDED STRAIGHT FORWARD and the legs trailing straight behind, wings broad with fingered primaries. A retracted neck is WRONG. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a heron (neck extended in flight, bustle over the tail), NOT a stork (no red bill, no white body), NOT a Sandhill Crane.
hirundo-rustica: Barn Swallow, adult (Hirundo rustica). MANDATORY: (1) A DEEP BRICK-RED FOREHEAD PATCH above the bill AND A DEEP BRICK-RED THROAT - both must be present and clearly red, not orange-buff, not white; (2) A BROAD GLOSSY BLUE-BLACK BREAST BAND separating the red throat from the pale underparts, complete or nearly complete across the chest - this band is diagnostic; (3) UNDERPARTS below the band CREAM to warm buff-white; (4) UPPERPARTS GLOSSY STEEL BLUE-BLACK, one flat zone with a slight sheen; (5) TAIL DEEPLY FORKED with VERY LONG THIN OUTER STREAMERS extending well beyond the rest of the tail, and a row of small WHITE SPOTS across the tail feathers; (6) WINGS long, narrow, and sharply pointed; (7) BILL minute and black with a wide gape; (8) LEGS tiny and dark, barely visible. FLIGHT POSE: streamers trailing as two fine lines, wings swept back, red throat and dark breast band still readable from below. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a House Martin (no white rump, no white throat, tail must have streamers), NOT a Sand Martin (not brown, no plain breast band on sandy ground), NOT a Tree Swallow (which has clean white underparts and a notched tail with no streamers). If the throat is white or the tail lacks streamers, the output is WRONG.
lagopus-lagopus: Willow Ptarmigan / Willow Grouse, ADULT MALE IN SUMMER PLUMAGE (Lagopus lagopus). Render the summer bird: (1) HEAD, NECK, AND BREAST RICH CHESTNUT-RUFOUS BROWN, with fine dark barring abstracted into 2-3 broad zones; (2) WINGS AND BELLY PURE WHITE, retained year-round - the contrast between a rufous front end and WHITE WINGS is THE diagnostic combination and must be a hard flat edge; (3) A SMALL BRIGHT SCARLET COMB / WATTLE above each eye, drawn as a small red crescent; (4) BILL SHORT, DEEP, BLACK, and slightly hooked - a stubby gamebird bill; (5) LEGS AND FEET DENSELY FEATHERED WHITE right down over the toes, so the legs read as thick white boots with tiny dark claws; (6) BODY PLUMP, ROUND-BACKED, and SHORT-TAILED with a small head; (7) TAIL BLACK, mostly hidden by white coverts. FLIGHT POSE: whirring shallow wingbeats, wings short and rounded and WHITE, body rufous. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Rock Ptarmigan (no black eye-stripe through the eye), NOT a Black Grouse or Capercaillie (not black, no lyre tail), NOT a partridge or pheasant. If the wings are brown, the output is WRONG.
linaria-cannabina: Common Linnet, breeding adult MALE (Linaria cannabina). MANDATORY: (1) A CRIMSON-PINK FORECROWN PATCH on the forehead and front of the crown, and a SEPARATE CRIMSON-PINK WASH ON EACH SIDE OF THE BREAST - two distinct pink zones, one on the head and one on the chest, with the throat between them left pale; (2) HEAD OTHERWISE PLAIN SOFT GREY - grey crown sides, grey nape, grey face with a pale patch around the eye and a pale throat marked with fine dark streaks; (3) BACK AND WING COVERTS UNSTREAKED WARM CHESTNUT-BROWN, a clean flat rufous zone; (4) BILL SMALL, SHORT, and GREY, conical; (5) WINGS dark with WHITE EDGES to the primaries forming a pale flash; (6) TAIL fairly long and NOTCHED with broad WHITE EDGES to the outer feathers; (7) BELLY pale buff-white; (8) LEGS brown, slim. SHAPE: slim, small-headed, longer-tailed and less round than a redpoll. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Common Redpoll (which has a BLACK CHIN SPOT, a streaked back, a tiny yellow bill, and pale wingbars), NOT a Twite (no yellow bill, no plain buff face), NOT a rosefinch (no pink hood). If a black chin spot appears or the back is streaked, the output is WRONG.
lophophanes-cristatus: European Crested Tit, adult (Lophophanes cristatus). MANDATORY: (1) A TALL, POINTED, TRIANGULAR CREST rising from the crown, SPECKLED BLACK AND WHITE, held erect - the crest is the species and must be sharp and clearly pointed, never a soft rounded bump; (2) FACE WHITISH, crossed by a CURVED BLACK LINE that runs from behind the eye, back, then DOWN AND FORWARD around the ear-coverts in a C-shape, forming a black crescent enclosing the white cheek; (3) A NARROW BLACK COLLAR running around the side of the neck, joining a SMALL BLACK BIB under the chin; (4) UPPERPARTS PLAIN WARM GREY-BROWN with NO wingbars and NO streaking; (5) UNDERPARTS off-white washed warm buff on the flanks; (6) BILL very short, black, conical; (7) EYE dark and prominent in the white face; (8) LEGS blue-grey, short. SHAPE: small, compact, large-headed because of the crest. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Tufted Titmouse (which is plain grey with a soft grey crest and no black face lines), NOT a Coal Tit (no crest, white nape patch), NOT a Blue Tit. If the crest is absent or rounded, or the face lacks the black crescent, the output is WRONG.
loxia-leucoptera: Two-barred Crossbill / White-winged Crossbill, adult MALE (Loxia leucoptera). MANDATORY: (1) THE BILL TIPS CROSS - the upper and lower mandibles overlap sideways at the tip, and this crossing must be clearly visible in profile; a straight conical bill is WRONG; (2) TWO BROAD, CLEAN, WHITE WING BARS across each dark wing, plus white tips to the tertials - these bold white bars on black are THE diagnostic mark and must be wide and obvious, not thin lines; (3) BODY RASPBERRY-PINK to rose-red overall in the male, brightest on the rump and breast, with a slightly darker back; (4) WINGS AND TAIL BLACKISH; (5) TAIL SHORT and DEEPLY NOTCHED; (6) HEAD LARGE with a THICK BULL NECK and a heavy front-loaded look; (7) LEGS short, dark, and strong; (8) BODY compact and chunky. STYLE: the wing is ONE flat black shape with TWO bold white strokes across it. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Common or Parrot Crossbill (which have NO white wing bars at all), NOT a Pine Grosbeak (which is larger with a stubby curved bill and only thin wing bars), NOT a rosefinch. If the wings lack two broad white bars, or the bill tips do not cross, the output is WRONG.
mergus-merganser: Common Merganser / Goosander, breeding adult MALE (Mergus merganser). MANDATORY: (1) HEAD GLOSSY DARK BOTTLE-GREEN, appearing black at a distance, with a slightly shaggy rear crown but NO wispy double crest; (2) BILL LONG, THIN, and BRIGHT RED-ORANGE with a HOOKED NAIL AT THE TIP and a SERRATED edge - draw the bill narrow and cylindrical, clearly unlike a duck's flat spatulate bill; this narrow red bill is diagnostic; (3) BODY LONG, LOW, and CIGAR-SHAPED, sitting deep; (4) BREAST, FLANKS, AND BELLY CREAMY WHITE, often with a soft peach-pink flush, as one flat pale zone; (5) BACK BLACK, contrasting sharply with the white flanks in a clean flat edge; (6) A NARROW BLACK EYE and no white cheek patch; (7) LEGS AND WEBBED FEET ORANGE-RED, set far back; (8) TAIL short and grey. FLIGHT POSE: the body is held straight and level with head, neck, and body in one line, wings showing LARGE WHITE INNER-WING PANELS crossed by a thin black line. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Red-breasted Merganser (no spiky double crest, no rusty speckled breast band, no white neck ring), NOT a Mallard (bill is narrow and red, not broad and yellow), NOT a cormorant.
motacilla-alba: White Wagtail, breeding adult (Motacilla alba). MANDATORY: (1) A CLEAN THREE-TONE HEAD - WHITE FOREHEAD AND FACE, a BLACK CROWN AND NAPE running back over the head, and a LARGE BLACK BIB covering the chin, throat, and upper breast; the white face is surrounded by black above and below; (2) BACK, MANTLE, AND RUMP CLEAN MID-GREY, one flat zone; (3) UNDERPARTS below the black bib WHITE; (4) WINGS BLACKISH with BOLD WHITE EDGES to the coverts forming TWO clean white bars; (5) TAIL VERY LONG, BLACK, with WHITE OUTER FEATHERS on each side - and the tail is a defining proportion: long, narrow, and constantly pumped; (6) BILL FINE, straight, and BLACK; (7) LEGS THIN and BLACK; (8) BODY SLENDER and held HORIZONTAL, walking rather than hopping. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Grey Wagtail (which has a YELLOW rump and undertail and PINK-BROWN legs), NOT a Pied Flycatcher, NOT a chickadee. Keep all colour out of this bird: it is black, white, and grey ONLY, with no yellow anywhere. If any yellow appears, the output is WRONG.
motacilla-cinerea: Grey Wagtail, breeding adult MALE (Motacilla cinerea). MANDATORY: (1) BACK, MANTLE, AND CROWN BLUE-GREY, and the RUMP BRIGHT YELLOW-GREEN - the grey back with a yellow-green rump is diagnostic; (2) UNDERTAIL COVERTS AND VENT VIVID LEMON-YELLOW, with the yellow strongest at the rear of the bird, fading paler on the belly and breast; (3) A BLACK THROAT PATCH in the breeding male, bordered above by a WHITE MOUSTACHIAL STRIPE running back from the bill and a WHITE SUPERCILIUM above the eye; (4) LEGS PALE PINK-BROWN, not black - the leg colour separates it from every other wagtail here; (5) TAIL EXTREMELY LONG, longer than any other wagtail, black with white outer feathers, held low and pumped constantly; (6) BILL fine, straight, dark; (7) BODY very slender and horizontal. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a White Wagtail (which has NO yellow anywhere and BLACK legs), NOT a Yellow Wagtail (which has an OLIVE-GREEN back and a YELLOW head, not a grey back and grey crown). The grey upperparts must never be replaced with green, and the yellow must be concentrated at the vent and rump. If the back is green or the legs are black, the output is WRONG.
muscicapa-striata: Spotted Flycatcher, adult (Muscicapa striata). THIS IS AN EXTREMELY PLAIN BIRD - do not invent markings. MANDATORY: (1) UPPERPARTS UNIFORM DULL MOUSE-GREY-BROWN with no wingbars, no supercilium, no eye-line, and no pattern of any kind; (2) FOREHEAD AND CROWN marked with FINE DARK STREAKS, drawn as 3-4 short hair-thin strokes ONLY, and the streaking stops at the crown - the face is plain; (3) UPPER BREAST washed grey-buff with SOFT DIFFUSE BLURRED STREAKS, at most 5 faint short strokes, fading to a clean off-white belly; (4) EYE LARGE, DARK, and ROUND on a plain pale face, with a faint pale eye-ring - the big dark eye on a blank face is the main character cue; (5) BILL BROAD-BASED, FLAT, and TRIANGULAR seen from above, dark with a pale base, surrounded by fine rictal bristles; (6) POSTURE STRICTLY UPRIGHT AND VERTICAL, body held erect on VERY SHORT dark legs, wings drooped slightly; (7) WINGS LONG, reaching well down the tail; TAIL medium and plain. STYLE OVERRIDE: this bird is 2 flat zones plus fewer than 10 marks total. Any dense stippling is WRONG. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a thrush (no bold breast spots), NOT a Pied Flycatcher (no black and white), NOT a phoebe.
nucifraga-caryocatactes: Spotted Nutcracker, adult (Nucifraga caryocatactes). MANDATORY: (1) BODY DEEP CHOCOLATE-BROWN covered ALL OVER with BOLD WHITE TEARDROP SPOTS on the breast, belly, flanks, mantle, and wing coverts - the spotting is DENSE and must be a scatter of 25 or more clean flat white drops, not a handful; (2) THE CROWN AND NAPE ARE PLAIN UNSPOTTED DARK BROWN, forming a clean brown cap above the spotted face and neck - this unspotted cap over a spotted body is diagnostic; (3) WINGS AND TAIL BLACKISH, largely unspotted; (4) A BROAD WHITE TIP TO THE TAIL and PURE WHITE UNDERTAIL COVERTS, forming a bright white rear end that must be visible in both poses; (5) BILL LONG, STRAIGHT, POINTED, and BLACK, dagger-like rather than crow-like, roughly 1.5 times the head depth; (6) HEAD LARGE, body chunky, TAIL SHORT and squared; (7) LEGS black and strong. STYLE: 2 flat brown-and-black zones with the white spots as small confident dots - the spots are the only fine detail permitted. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Clark's Nutcracker (which is pale grey with black-and-white wings and no spots), NOT a starling (bill is long and straight, body is brown), NOT a woodpecker. If the body is sparsely spotted or grey, the output is WRONG.
panurus-biarmicus: Bearded Reedling, adult MALE (Panurus biarmicus). MANDATORY: (1) A BROAD BLACK MOUSTACHE hanging from below the eye DOWN the side of the throat as a thick WEDGE that widens as it descends - it is a drooping triangular blot, NOT a thin line and NOT a horizontal stripe; this is the single diagnostic mark; (2) HEAD PALE BLUE-GREY, clean and unmarked apart from the moustache; (3) BODY WARM TAWNY-ORANGE / CINNAMON across the back, breast, and flanks, one flat zone; (4) BILL SHORT, CONICAL, and BRIGHT ORANGE-YELLOW; (5) EYE pale yellow with a small dark pupil; (6) TAIL VERY LONG and GRADUATED, warm tawny, longer than the body, held low; (7) UNDERTAIL COVERTS BLACK in the male; (8) WINGS tawny with black-and-white edging on the flight feathers, abstracted to 2-3 flat strokes; (9) LEGS black, short. SHAPE: tiny round body with a disproportionately long tail. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Long-tailed Tit (which is a white-headed black-and-pink ball with a black tail), NOT a tit or chickadee, NOT a shrike (the moustache is a soft drooping wedge, not a mask through the eye). If the moustache runs horizontally through the eye, the output is WRONG.
parus-major: Great Tit, adult MALE (Parus major). MANDATORY: (1) HEAD GLOSSY BLACK - crown, nape, chin, and throat - with a LARGE CLEAN WHITE OVAL CHEEK PATCH on each side, fully enclosed by black above, behind, and below; the white cheek must be a bold flat oval, not a stripe; (2) A BROAD BLACK STRIPE RUNNING FROM THE BLACK BIB STRAIGHT DOWN THE CENTRE OF THE YELLOW BELLY to the vent, WIDE and unbroken in the male - this central black stripe is diagnostic and must be drawn as a bold flat band; (3) UNDERPARTS BRIGHT LEMON-YELLOW on either side of the stripe; (4) BACK OLIVE-GREEN; (5) WINGS AND TAIL BLUE-GREY, the wing crossed by ONE clean WHITE BAR; (6) A WHITE PATCH ON THE NAPE at the back of the black head; (7) BILL short, stout, black; (8) LEGS blue-grey. SIZE: the largest tit, chunky and thick-necked. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Blue Tit (no blue cap, no white ring around a blue crown, no eye-line), NOT a Coal Tit (no white nape patch alone, no thin bill), NOT a chickadee. If the belly stripe is missing or the crown is blue, the output is WRONG.
periparus-ater: Coal Tit, adult (Periparus ater). MANDATORY: (1) A LARGE CLEAN WHITE PATCH ON THE NAPE, sitting in the middle of the black hindneck like a white wedge running from the crown down toward the back - this white nape patch is THE diagnostic mark and must be clearly visible; (2) HEAD GLOSSY BLACK on the crown, chin, and throat, with LARGE WHITE CHEEK PATCHES on the sides; (3) THE BLACK BIB EXTENDS DOWN ONTO THE UPPER BREAST, larger than a Marsh Tit's neat chin patch; (4) UPPERPARTS PLAIN OLIVE-GREY with NO green and NO blue; (5) UNDERPARTS off-white washed warm buff on the flanks, with NO central belly stripe; (6) TWO THIN WHITE WING BARS across the grey wing, formed by white tips to the coverts; (7) BILL FINE, SHARP, and slender - noticeably thinner than a Great Tit's stout bill; (8) SMALL, ROUND, big-headed, and SHORT-TAILED. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Great Tit (no yellow underparts, no belly stripe, much smaller), NOT a Marsh Tit (which has NO white nape patch and NO wing bars), NOT a Crested Tit (no crest). If the nape has no white patch or the wings have no bars, the output is WRONG.
phasianus-colchicus: Common Pheasant, adult MALE (Phasianus colchicus). MANDATORY: (1) TAIL EXTREMELY LONG, POINTED, and BARRED - at least as long as the head and body combined, tapering to a fine point, warm buff with clean dark cross-bars abstracted to 6-8 flat bars; if the tail is short, the output is WRONG; (2) HEAD AND NECK GLOSSY DARK BOTTLE-GREEN with a purple sheen, drawn as one flat dark iridescent zone; (3) A LARGE BARE SCARLET FACE WATTLE surrounding the eye and cheek, drawn as a bold flat red mask; (4) SMALL EAR-TUFTS raised at the back of the crown; (5) A CLEAN WHITE NECK RING at the base of the green neck (in ring-necked stock); (6) BODY COPPER-GOLD to chestnut, marked with BLACK CRESCENTS - abstract this scaling into 2-3 broad zones with a scatter of at most 10 dark marks, never feather-by-feather; (7) RUMP and lower back blue-grey to olive; (8) LEGS grey, sturdy, with a short spur; (9) BILL short, pale horn, gamebird-shaped. FLIGHT POSE: explosive, wings short, broad and rounded, long tail streaming straight behind. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Golden Pheasant (no yellow crest, no red body, no orange cape), NOT a Grouse or Partridge.
phoenicurus-ochruros: Black Redstart, adult MALE (Phoenicurus ochruros). MANDATORY: (1) FACE, THROAT, AND BREAST SOOTY BLACK, blending into a DARK SLATE-GREY crown, back, and belly - the whole front and top of the bird is dark, with NO white forehead and NO orange breast; (2) THE RUMP AND TAIL BRIGHT RUST-ORANGE, contrasting hard against the dark body - this orange tail on a dark body is the whole species and must be a clean flat zone; (3) THE TWO CENTRAL TAIL FEATHERS ARE DARKER BROWN, so the tail reads as orange with a darker central line; (4) A PALE WHITE-GREY PANEL on the folded wing in adult males, drawn as a small flat pale block; (5) BILL fine, straight, and black; (6) LEGS THIN and BLACK; (7) POSTURE upright and alert with the TAIL QUIVERED and often flicked - draw it slightly raised; (8) BODY compact, robin-shaped, with a fairly large dark eye on a dark face. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Common Redstart (which has a WHITE FOREHEAD BAND, a BLUE-GREY crown and back, and a BRIGHT ORANGE BREAST), NOT a European Robin. If the breast is orange or the forehead is white, the output is WRONG.
phoenicurus-phoenicurus: Common Redstart, breeding adult MALE (Phoenicurus phoenicurus). MANDATORY: (1) A CLEAN WHITE BAND ACROSS THE FOREHEAD, above the bill and running back over the eye as a short white supercilium - this white forehead is diagnostic and must be a crisp flat white stripe; (2) A BLACK FACE AND THROAT forming a bib below the white forehead; (3) CROWN, NAPE, AND BACK SOFT BLUE-GREY, one flat zone; (4) BREAST AND FLANKS BRIGHT ORANGE-RUST, fading to paler on the belly; (5) RUMP AND TAIL BRIGHT RUST-ORANGE with DARKER BROWN CENTRAL TAIL FEATHERS; (6) BILL fine, straight, black; (7) LEGS thin and dark; (8) POSTURE upright, slim, with the ORANGE TAIL CONSTANTLY QUIVERED - draw the tail slightly lowered and shivering. THE COLOUR HIERARCHY: grey above, black face, white forehead, orange below and behind. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Black Redstart (which is sooty black and slate all over with NO white forehead and NO orange breast), NOT a European Robin (which has no white forehead, no grey back, and no orange tail). If the forehead lacks white or the back is brown, the output is WRONG.
phylloscopus-collybita: Common Chiffchaff, adult (Phylloscopus collybita). This species is separated from Willow Warbler by small details - get them exactly right. MANDATORY: (1) LEGS DARK BLACKISH-BROWN, nearly black - this is the single most reliable mark and must be clearly dark; (2) UPPERPARTS DULL GREY-OLIVE, colder and drabber than a Willow Warbler, with no wingbars and no streaking; (3) UNDERPARTS DIRTY OFF-WHITE washed buff on the breast sides, never clean lemon; (4) A SHORT, FAINT, INDISTINCT PALE SUPERCILIUM that barely extends past the eye, plus a DARK EYE-STRIPE and a THIN DARK EYE-RING that gives a beady-eyed look; (5) WINGS SHORT AND ROUNDED, with the folded wingtip falling only a short way down the tail; (6) BILL FINE, thin, and mostly DARK with a paler base; (7) BODY small and rounded with a slightly rounded crown; (8) tail dipped downward in a habitual flick. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Willow Warbler (which has PALE PINK-BROWN legs, a LONGER CLEARER SUPERCILIUM, cleaner yellow-and-green tones, and LONGER more pointed wings). If the legs are pale, the output is WRONG. STYLE: 2 flat zones and fewer than 8 marks total on the whole bird.
phylloscopus-trochilus: Willow Warbler, adult (Phylloscopus trochilus). MANDATORY: (1) LEGS PALE PINK-BROWN to straw-coloured, clearly LIGHT - this is the key separator from Chiffchaff and must be drawn pale; (2) UPPERPARTS CLEAN OLIVE-GREEN, brighter and warmer than a Chiffchaff, with no wingbars; (3) UNDERPARTS WASHED CLEAN LEMON-YELLOW on the throat and breast, fading to white on the belly - noticeably yellower than a Chiffchaff; (4) A LONG, CLEAR, PALE YELLOW SUPERCILIUM running well BEHIND the eye, above a distinct dark eye-stripe - this bold eyebrow gives a gentle, open-faced expression; (5) WINGS LONG AND POINTED, with the folded wingtip reaching well down the tail - a long primary projection; (6) BILL fine, pointed, with a PALE ORANGE-HORN LOWER MANDIBLE; (7) BODY slim and elegant with a flat-crowned head. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Chiffchaff (dark legs, short weak supercilium, short rounded wings, drab grey-olive tones), NOT a Wood Warbler (which has a bright yellow throat cut off sharply from a pure white belly), NOT a New World warbler. If the legs are dark or the face lacks a clear pale eyebrow, the output is WRONG. STYLE: 2 flat zones, fewer than 8 marks total.
pica-pica: Eurasian Magpie, adult (Pica pica). PROPORTION FIRST: the TAIL IS LONGER THAN THE HEAD AND BODY COMBINED, graduated to a point, and must dominate the silhouette. MANDATORY: (1) HEAD, NECK, BREAST, BACK, AND RUMP SOLID BLACK; (2) A LARGE CLEAN WHITE BELLY PATCH on the lower breast and flanks, and a LARGE WHITE OVAL SCAPULAR PATCH on each shoulder - two distinct white blocks against black, both must be bold and flat-edged; (3) THE PRIMARIES are largely WHITE with black tips, so in the flight pose each spread wing shows a BIG WHITE PANEL near the tip; (4) TAIL AND WING BLACK WITH GREEN-BLUE-PURPLE IRIDESCENCE, rendered as one flat sheen zone over the black, never as gradient shading; (5) BILL BLACK, stout, slightly hooked; (6) EYE dark; (7) LEGS BLACK and sturdy. STYLE: this bird is FOUR flat zones - black, white belly, white shoulder, iridescent tail. NO feather-by-feather rendering. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Black-billed Magpie of North America rendered with different proportions, NOT a jay (no blue body, no barred wing panel, no white rump), NOT a crow. If the tail is shorter than the body or the shoulder ovals are missing, the output is WRONG.
picus-viridis: European Green Woodpecker, adult MALE (Picus viridis). MANDATORY: (1) UPPERPARTS AND WINGS DULL OLIVE-GREEN, one flat zone, with a BRIGHT GOLDEN-YELLOW RUMP that must be visible, especially in the flight pose; (2) A BRIGHT CRIMSON CROWN running from the forehead back over the whole top of the head to the nape; (3) A BOLD BLACK FACE MASK surrounding the eye and lores, giving a bandit look; (4) A MOUSTACHIAL STRIPE below the eye that is BLACK WITH A RED CENTRE in the male - draw the red core inside the black wedge; (5) EYE PALE WHITE-BLUE with a small dark pupil, staring out of the black mask - this pale eye is diagnostic; (6) UNDERPARTS PALE GREY-GREEN, plain, with at most a few faint bars on the vent; (7) BILL long, straight, chisel-tipped, grey; (8) LEGS grey, zygodactyl; (9) TAIL stiff, olive with faint dark bars, braced downward. POSE 1: upright and clinging to an implied vertical surface, tail as a prop. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Northern Flicker (no black bib crescent, no spotted belly, no brown barred back), NOT a Grey-headed Woodpecker (which has a grey head, only a small red forehead, and a much fainter moustache). If the belly is spotted or the crown is only partly red, the output is WRONG.
poecile-palustris: Marsh Tit, adult (Poecile palustris). This bird is defined by what it lacks - keep it clean and minimal. MANDATORY: (1) A GLOSSY BLACK CAP covering the crown and nape, ending in a NEAT SHARP LINE just above the eye, and the cap is SHINY, not matt; (2) A SMALL, NEAT, TIDY BLACK BIB under the chin - a compact black wedge that does NOT spread down onto the breast; (3) CHEEKS AND SIDES OF NECK CLEAN WHITE, brightest just behind the bill; (4) UPPERPARTS PLAIN WARM GREY-BROWN with NO WING BARS AND NO PALE WING PANEL - the folded wing is one uniform flat brown shape with no markings whatsoever; (5) UNDERPARTS off-white with buff flanks, plain; (6) NO WHITE NAPE PATCH - the black cap runs uninterrupted onto the brown back; (7) BILL SHORT, stout, and BLACK, with a small pale spot at the base of the upper mandible; (8) LEGS dark blue-grey. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Coal Tit (which has a bold WHITE NAPE PATCH and TWO WHITE WING BARS), NOT a Willow Tit (which has a matt sooty cap, a larger diffuse bib, and a pale wing panel), NOT a Blackcap (this is a tit with a stubby bill, not a warbler). If any wing bar or nape patch appears, the output is WRONG.
pyrrhula-pyrrhula: Eurasian Bullfinch, adult MALE (Pyrrhula pyrrhula). MANDATORY: (1) A GLOSSY BLACK CAP covering the crown, forehead, face, and CHIN, wrapping around the base of the bill like a black hood pulled forward - the black surrounds the bill and includes the lores and chin; (2) CHEEKS, BREAST, AND BELLY BRIGHT ROSE-PINK / VERMILION, a large clean flat zone reaching from just below the black chin down to the vent; (3) BACK AND MANTLE SOFT BLUE-GREY; (4) A BRILLIANT PURE WHITE RUMP forming a broad flat band between the grey back and the BLACK TAIL - this white rump is diagnostic and must be bold in both poses; (5) WINGS BLACK with ONE clean pale grey-white BAR across the coverts; (6) UNDERTAIL COVERTS WHITE; (7) BILL VERY SHORT, DEEP, STUBBY, and BLACK, with a strongly curved culmen and almost no point - a bull-headed bill; (8) BODY ROUND with a THICK BULL NECK and a large head; LEGS dark, short. STYLE: 5 flat zones and nothing else. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a rosefinch (no black hood, no white rump, bill is stubby), NOT a Pine Grosbeak, NOT a redpoll. If the rump is not white or the bill is conical and pointed, the output is WRONG.
rallus-aquaticus: Water Rail, adult (Rallus aquaticus). MANDATORY: (1) BILL LONG, SLENDER, and SLIGHTLY DOWNCURVED, roughly 1.5 times the head length, ORANGE-RED at the base fading to dark at the tip - this long red bill is diagnostic and separates it from every crake; (2) FACE, THROAT, AND BREAST SOFT BLUE-GREY, a clean flat zone; (3) CROWN AND UPPERPARTS OLIVE-BROWN with BOLD BLACK STREAKS, abstracted to 4-5 broad dark strokes over 2 flat zones; (4) FLANKS BARRED BLACK AND WHITE in clean vertical bars - draw 5-7 confident flat strokes, never dense hatching; (5) UNDERTAIL COVERTS CREAM-WHITE, often flicked upward; (6) BODY LATERALLY COMPRESSED and narrow, so it reads as a thin slab from the front, with a distinctly hunched, skulking posture; (7) LEGS LONG, PINK-BROWN, with VERY LONG SPREADING TOES; (8) TAIL short and cocked; EYE red-brown. POSTURE: crouched, head lowered, moving through implied reeds. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Corncrake or Spotted Crake (bill must be long and red, not short and stubby), NOT a moorhen (no red frontal shield, no white flank line), NOT a Virginia Rail. If the bill is short, the output is WRONG.
regulus-regulus: Goldcrest, adult MALE (Regulus regulus). SIZE AND SHAPE: the smallest bird in this whole set - a nearly spherical body, a large round head, an almost invisible neck, and a very short tail. MANDATORY: (1) A BRIGHT ORANGE-YELLOW CROWN STRIPE running front to back along the top of the head, BORDERED ON EACH SIDE BY A CLEAN BLACK LINE - the black-yellow-black crown sandwich is THE diagnostic mark and must be crisp; (2) FACE PLAIN PALE GREY-BUFF with NO supercilium and NO eye-stripe, but with a LARGE DARK EYE set in a PALE SURROUND, giving a wide-eyed, blank-faced look; (3) UPPERPARTS SOFT OLIVE-GREEN; (4) UNDERPARTS dull buff-white; (5) WINGS with TWO WHITE BARS and a distinct BLACK BAR just below the lower white bar; (6) BILL EXTREMELY FINE, short, needle-like, and black; (7) LEGS very thin, brownish, with yellowish feet; (8) posture restless and hovering. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Firecrest (which has a BOLD WHITE SUPERCILIUM and a BLACK EYE-STRIPE and a bronze shoulder patch - the Goldcrest's face is PLAIN), NOT a warbler or kinglet with a striped face. If the face has an eyebrow stripe, the output is WRONG. STYLE: 3 flat zones plus the crown stripe. Fewer than 10 marks total.
riparia-riparia: Sand Martin / Bank Swallow, adult (Riparia riparia). MANDATORY: (1) UPPERPARTS PLAIN SANDY GREY-BROWN with NO GLOSS, NO BLUE, and NO IRIDESCENCE anywhere - a matt, dusty brown bird; (2) UNDERPARTS WHITE, crossed by a DISTINCT BROWN BREAST BAND running right across the chest, with the WHITE THROAT ABOVE IT clean and separate - the brown band on a white front is THE diagnostic mark and must be drawn clearly in both poses; (3) TAIL SHORT and SHALLOWLY NOTCHED, with NO streamers and NO deep fork; (4) RUMP BROWN, the same as the back - no white rump patch; (5) WINGS narrow, pointed, and brown; (6) BILL minute and black; (7) LEGS tiny, dark, and BARE - no feathering; (8) BODY SMALL and slight, the smallest of the swallows and martins. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a House Martin (which has a BOLD WHITE RUMP, blue-black upperparts, an all-white underside with NO breast band, and white-feathered legs), NOT a Barn Swallow (no red throat, no tail streamers, no blue gloss), NOT a Tree Swallow. If the upperparts are blue or glossy, or the breast band is missing, the output is WRONG.
saxicola-rubicola: European Stonechat, breeding adult MALE (Saxicola rubicola). MANDATORY: (1) HEAD ENTIRELY BLACK - crown, face, and throat as one solid black hood; (2) A BOLD WHITE HALF-COLLAR on EACH SIDE OF THE NECK, sitting between the black head and the dark back, and NOT meeting across the nape - two white side patches, not a ring; (3) BREAST DEEP ORANGE-RUST, brightest on the upper chest, fading to buff-white on the belly; (4) BACK DARK BROWN-BLACK with heavy mottling abstracted to 2 flat zones; (5) A SMALL WHITE WING PATCH on the inner wing coverts, drawn as a clean flat white block; (6) RUMP dark and streaked, NOT white - in this species the rump is not a white flash; (7) BODY VERY UPRIGHT AND ROUND, with a SHORT TAIL and a big head, perched high with the chest thrust out; (8) BILL short, fine, black; LEGS short and black. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Whinchat (which has a BOLD CREAM SUPERCILIUM over the eye and a brown streaked head - the Stonechat's head is plain solid black with no eyebrow), NOT a European Robin (which has no black hood and no white neck patches). If a pale eyebrow appears, the output is WRONG.
scolopax-rusticola: Eurasian Woodcock, adult (Scolopax rusticola). MANDATORY: (1) HUGE BLACK EYES SET VERY HIGH AND FAR BACK ON THE HEAD, near the top rear of the skull - this eye placement is diagnostic and gives the bird a distinctive top-heavy, wide-eyed head; draw the eyes larger than seems natural; (2) THREE OR FOUR BOLD DARK TRANSVERSE BARS ACROSS THE REAR CROWN AND NAPE, running SIDE TO SIDE like rungs, NOT front to back - crown bars running lengthwise are WRONG and would make it a snipe; (3) BILL LONG, STRAIGHT, and STOUT, pinkish-grey with a darker tip, held angled downward; (4) BODY BULKY, ROUND-BACKED, and HEAVY, standing LOW on VERY SHORT grey-pink legs; (5) PLUMAGE dead-leaf camouflage - warm russet, buff, grey, and black, abstracted into 3 broad flat zones with a scatter of at most 8 bold dark marks; (6) A DARK LINE FROM THE BILL TO THE EYE; (7) WINGS BROAD AND ROUNDED - in flight the bird looks owl-like and heavy, with the long bill pointing down. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a snipe (crown bars run crosswise, body far bulkier, legs shorter, eyes higher), NOT an American Woodcock. STYLE OVERRIDE: this plumage tempts feather-by-feather rendering.
