Broad flat zones only. Fewer than 10 dark marks total.
sitta-europaea: Eurasian Nuthatch, adult (Sitta europaea). POSTURE OVERRIDE: render the perched pose with the bird ON A VERTICAL IMPLIED SURFACE FACING HEAD-DOWN, body angled down the trunk, which is the diagnostic nuthatch posture and unique among these birds. MANDATORY: (1) UPPERPARTS CLEAN BLUE-GREY, one flat unmarked zone from crown to tail; (2) A BOLD BLACK STRIPE running from the bill THROUGH THE EYE and back to the side of the neck, thick and clean; (3) CHEEKS AND THROAT WHITE; (4) UNDERPARTS WARM BUFF-ORANGE, deepening to RICH CHESTNUT on the rear flanks and vent (in northern birds the underparts may be whiter, but keep chestnut on the flanks); (5) BILL LONG, STRAIGHT, POINTED, and CHISEL-LIKE, grey with a paler base, roughly head-length; (6) TAIL VERY SHORT and squared, so the body looks like a wedge with almost no tail; (7) NECK ABSENT - the head runs straight into the body in one dagger-shaped line; (8) LEGS SHORT and STOUT with LARGE STRONG TOES AND LONG CLAWS gripping the implied bark. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a treecreeper (which is brown, head-UP, with a curved bill and a long stiff tail), NOT a White-breasted Nuthatch (which has a black cap and white underparts), NOT a woodpecker. If the tail is long or the bird is head-up, the output is WRONG.
spinus-spinus: Eurasian Siskin, adult MALE (Spinus spinus). MANDATORY: (1) A SMALL BLACK CAP on the crown and forehead only, and a SMALL BLACK CHIN PATCH under the bill - two separate small black marks on an otherwise yellow-green head; (2) FACE, THROAT, AND BREAST BRIGHT YELLOW-GREEN, with a YELLOW SUPERCILIUM curving back over the eye and a yellow patch on the side of the neck; (3) BACK yellow-olive with fine dark streaks abstracted to 3 short strokes; (4) FLANKS whitish with FINE DARK STREAKS, at most 5 thin strokes; (5) WINGS BLACK with TWO BROAD BRIGHT YELLOW BARS - bold flat yellow bands across a black wing, plus yellow edges to the flight feathers; these yellow bars are diagnostic; (6) TAIL SHORT and DEEPLY NOTCHED with YELLOW PATCHES AT THE SIDES OF THE BASE; (7) BILL FINE, SHARPLY POINTED, and CONICAL, pale horn - noticeably slim and pointed for a finch; (8) BODY SMALL, compact, and short-tailed; LEGS dark. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Greenfinch (much smaller, streaked, black cap, thin bill), NOT an American Goldfinch (which has a white-and-black wing and an orange bill), NOT a Serin. If the wing bars are white or the cap is missing, the output is WRONG.
stercorarius-parasiticus: Parasitic Jaeger / Arctic Skua, breeding adult PALE MORPH (Stercorarius parasiticus). MANDATORY: (1) TWO ELONGATED CENTRAL TAIL FEATHERS projecting as a SINGLE FINE STRAIGHT POINT well beyond the rest of the tail, roughly a third of the tail length again - pointed, not spoon-tipped and not twisted; this pin-tail is diagnostic; (2) A DARK BROWN-BLACK CAP covering the crown and reaching down to just below the eye, sharply defined against a PALE STRAW-YELLOW WASHED NECK and cheek; (3) UNDERPARTS CREAM-WHITE with, at most, a faint smudged breast band; (4) UPPERPARTS UNIFORM DARK GREY-BROWN, one flat zone; (5) A PALE FLASH AT THE BASE OF THE PRIMARIES on each wing, visible as a white crescent near the wingtip in the flight pose - this white wing flash must be present; (6) BILL SHORT, DARK, and HOOKED at the tip with a visible cere-like sheath; (7) WINGS LONG, NARROW, and SHARPLY ANGLED, falcon-like; (8) LEGS AND FEET BLACK, webbed. FLIGHT POSE: buoyant, wings angled, body streamlined, pin-tail trailing. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a gull (dark cap, hooked bill, pointed wings, tail spike), NOT a Long-tailed Jaeger (whose streamers are far longer and more flexible), NOT a Great Skua (which is bulky with no tail spike).
streptopelia-decaocto: Eurasian Collared Dove, adult (Streptopelia decaocto). MANDATORY: (1) A NARROW BLACK HALF-COLLAR ACROSS THE BACK AND SIDES OF THE NECK, thinly edged in white above and below, NOT meeting at the front of the throat - a small crisp black crescent on the hindneck, and it is the only strong mark on the bird; (2) BODY UNIFORM PALE SANDY GREY-BUFF, warmer on the breast, paler on the head and belly - one soft flat wash over the whole bird with no pattern; (3) WINGTIPS DARKER GREY-BROWN, forming a soft dark edge to the folded wing; (4) TAIL LONG and SQUARE-ENDED, grey above, with a BROAD WHITE TERMINAL BAND AND BLACK BASE on the underside - the black-and-white undertail must show in the flight pose; (5) EYE DEEP RED-BROWN, small, set in a narrow bare white eye-ring; (6) BILL SLENDER, SHORT, and DARK GREY; (7) LEGS SHORT and DULL PINK-RED; (8) HEAD SMALL AND ROUNDED on a slim neck, body slender and long-tailed. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Wood Pigeon (no white neck patch, no white wing slash, far slimmer), NOT a Rock Dove (no wing bars, no white rump, not grey), NOT a Mourning Dove (tail square, not pointed). If the bird is blue-grey or the collar runs across the throat, the output is WRONG.
strix-aluco: Tawny Owl, adult (Strix aluco). MANDATORY: (1) EYES ENTIRELY BLACK - large, round, deep black with no visible iris colour; this is THE diagnostic feature and any yellow or orange in the eye makes it the wrong species; (2) HEAD VERY LARGE AND PERFECTLY ROUND with NO EAR TUFTS; (3) A BROAD SOFT FACIAL DISC in warm buff-grey, bounded by a soft pale ring, with TWO PALE VERTICAL STRIPES running down between the eyes on either side of the bill forming a pale X-shape on the forehead; (4) PLUMAGE warm russet-brown mottled with dark, abstracted into 2-3 broad flat zones with a scatter of pale marks - never feather-by-feather; (5) UNDERPARTS paler buff with BOLD DARK VERTICAL STREAKS running down the breast, drawn as 5-7 confident dark strokes, each with faint cross-bars; (6) A ROW OF PALE SPOTS along the outer edge of the folded wing forming a pale shoulder line; (7) BILL small, pale yellow-horn, mostly hidden in facial feathers; (8) BODY BARREL-SHAPED, thickset, short-tailed, with FEATHERED LEGS ending in strong pale toes. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Long-eared Owl (no ear tufts, no orange eyes), NOT a Barn Owl (not white, disc is round not heart-shaped), NOT a Tengmalm's Owl (which has bright yellow eyes and a white-framed disc).
sylvia-atricapilla: Eurasian Blackcap, adult MALE (Sylvia atricapilla). MANDATORY: (1) A NEAT GLOSSY BLACK CAP CONFINED TO THE TOP OF THE HEAD, starting at the forehead and ENDING IN A CLEAN HORIZONTAL LINE LEVEL WITH THE EYE - the cap does NOT reach the nape, does NOT cover the cheek, and does NOT extend below the eye; it is a small skullcap, and its limited extent is the diagnostic point; (2) FACE, CHEEKS, AND THROAT SOFT ASH-GREY, plain and unmarked, with NO eyebrow, NO eye-ring, and NO eye-stripe; (3) UPPERPARTS PLAIN OLIVE-GREY-BROWN with no wingbars, no streaking, and no pattern of any kind; (4) UNDERPARTS PALE SILVER-GREY, plain; (5) BILL FINE, THIN, and POINTED, dark grey - a warbler bill, not a conical finch bill; (6) LEGS blue-grey, slim; (7) TAIL medium, plain, and unmarked; (8) BODY slim and neat with a rather flat crown. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Marsh Tit or any tit (whose black cap runs back over the NAPE and pairs with a black bib and a stubby bill), NOT a Bullfinch (no pink breast, no white rump), NOT a Blackpoll Warbler. If the black extends to the nape or below the eye, or a black bib appears, the output is WRONG.
tringa-glareola: Wood Sandpiper, breeding adult (Tringa glareola). MANDATORY: (1) UPPERPARTS DARK BROWN DENSELY SPANGLED WITH PALE CREAM SPOTS, giving a spotted, checkered look across the back and wings - abstract to a flat brown zone carrying a scatter of 15-20 clean pale dots, which is the diagnostic pattern; (2) A LONG, CLEAR, WHITE SUPERCILIUM running from the bill well BEHIND THE EYE, bold and unmistakable, above a dark eye-stripe; (3) NECK AND UPPER BREAST finely streaked grey-brown, fading into a CLEAN WHITE BELLY - the boundary is soft, not a hard band; (4) LEGS LONG and BRIGHT YELLOW-GREEN, and in the flight pose THE FEET PROJECT WELL BEYOND THE TAIL TIP - this projection is diagnostic; (5) BILL STRAIGHT, fine, and dark, roughly head-length; (6) RUMP WHITE with a finely barred tail, visible in flight; (7) BODY SLIM AND ELEGANT with an upright stance and a small head. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Common Sandpiper (which is plain brown-backed, short-legged, low-slung with a white shoulder wedge), NOT a Green Sandpiper (which is much darker above with a bold white belly contrast and dark underwings), NOT a Spotted Sandpiper (no black breast spots). If the back is plain, the output is WRONG.
troglodytes-troglodytes: Eurasian Wren, adult (Troglodytes troglodytes). SHAPE IS THE SPECIES: a TINY, ROUND, ALMOST TAILLESS BALL with a SHORT STUBBY TAIL HELD COCKED STRAIGHT UP, near vertical, over the back. If the tail is not cocked upright, the output is WRONG. MANDATORY: (1) BODY RICH WARM RUFOUS-BROWN throughout; (2) FINE DARK BARRING on the wings, tail, and flanks, abstracted to 4-6 clean thin flat bars on the wing and tail only - the body itself stays flat and unbarred; (3) A PALE BUFF SUPERCILIUM above the eye on an otherwise plain face; (4) BILL FINE, slightly DOWNCURVED, and dark, roughly head-length; (5) THROAT AND BREAST paler buff, plain; (6) WINGS SHORT AND ROUNDED, held tight to the body; (7) LEGS PALE PINK-BROWN, surprisingly long and sturdy for the size, with the body carried in a crouched, forward-leaning posture; (8) HEAD large relative to the body with almost no neck. STYLE: 2 flat brown zones plus the bars. Fewer than 12 marks total. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a treecreeper (which is white below, head-up on a trunk, with a long stiff tail), NOT a dipper (which is far larger with a white bib). Keep it minute and round.
turdus-iliacus: Redwing, adult (Turdus iliacus). MANDATORY: (1) A BOLD CREAM-WHITE SUPERCILIUM running from the bill back over the eye to the nape, thick and unmistakable, PLUS A SECOND CREAM STRIPE running below the dark cheek from the bill along the lower edge of the ear-coverts - this double-striped face is THE diagnostic mark and must be drawn in both poses; (2) A RUST-RED PATCH ON THE FLANKS AND UNDERWING, sitting under the folded wing on the side of the body as a clean flat rust zone, which must show in the perched pose and blaze on the underwing in the flight pose; (3) UPPERPARTS PLAIN OLIVE-BROWN, unmarked; (4) UNDERPARTS CREAM-WHITE with BOLD DARK STREAKS running down the breast and flanks - streaks, drawn as 8-10 short confident strokes, NOT round spots; (5) BILL dark with a YELLOW BASE to the lower mandible; (6) LEGS pale pinkish-brown; (7) SIZE SMALL for a thrush, clearly smaller and neater than a Blackbird. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Song Thrush (which has a plain face with NO supercilium and round spots, and no rust flanks), NOT a Fieldfare (no grey head, no chestnut back), NOT an American Robin. If the face lacks the bold eyebrow or the flanks lack rust, the output is WRONG.
turdus-merula: Common Blackbird, adult MALE (Turdus merula). MANDATORY: (1) THE ENTIRE BODY IS UNIFORM MATT BLACK - head, back, wings, tail, breast, and belly as ONE flat black zone with NO sheen, NO iridescence, NO purple or green highlights, NO pale feather edges, and NO markings whatsoever; (2) THE BILL IS BRIGHT ORANGE-YELLOW, deep at the base and slightly downcurved - one of only two colour marks on the bird; (3) A NARROW BRIGHT YELLOW EYE-RING encircling a dark eye, drawn as a clean thin yellow ring - the second colour mark; (4) LEGS AND FEET DARK BROWN-BLACK, slim; (5) TAIL FAIRLY LONG and often held slightly raised or fanned on landing; (6) BODY the classic thrush shape - plump chest, upright alert stance, medium-length legs, rounded head. STYLE OVERRIDE: because the body is one flat black shape, the bill and eye-ring carry the entire image. Draw them crisply and let everything else stay flat. Do NOT add feather detail, wing bars, or texture to break up the black. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Common Starling (no spots, no short tail, no pointed yellow bill), NOT a Carrion Crow (far smaller with an orange bill), NOT an American Robin (no red breast, no grey back).
turdus-pilaris: Fieldfare, adult (Turdus pilaris). This bird is a THREE-COLOUR THRUSH and all three zones must be distinct. MANDATORY: (1) HEAD AND NAPE PALE BLUE-GREY, with a paler supercilium and small dark streaks on the crown; (2) MANTLE AND BACK RICH WARM CHESTNUT-BROWN, a clean flat zone that CONTRASTS SHARPLY with the grey head in front of it; (3) RUMP PALE BLUE-GREY, contrasting with a SOLID BLACK TAIL - so the sequence down the bird's back is GREY, CHESTNUT, GREY, BLACK, and this sequence is diagnostic; (4) BREAST GOLDEN-BUFF, heavily marked with BLACK ARROWHEAD OR CHEVRON SPOTS that thin out toward a WHITE BELLY - draw 10-12 confident dark chevrons, not round dots and not fine streaks; (5) FLANKS marked with black chevrons on white; (6) BILL YELLOW with a DARK TIP; (7) LEGS dark brown; (8) POSTURE UPRIGHT and bold, chest out, larger and longer-tailed than a Redwing. FLIGHT POSE: the WHITE UNDERWING LININGS flash pale, and the grey rump against the black tail is obvious. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Mistle Thrush (no grey head, no chestnut back, spots are chevrons not round blots), NOT a Redwing (no bold eyebrow, no rust flanks), NOT an American Robin.
turdus-viscivorus: Mistle Thrush, adult (Turdus viscivorus). MANDATORY: (1) UPPERPARTS COLD PALE GREY-BROWN, notably PALE and washed-out, with a faint frosted look and PALE EDGES to the wing coverts giving a scaly shoulder - never warm or rufous; (2) UNDERPARTS OFF-WHITE covered in LARGE, BOLD, ROUND-TO-OVAL BLACK BLOTCHES scattered evenly across the breast, belly, AND FLANKS - the spots are LARGE and SEPARATE, more like blots than streaks, and they run right down onto the flanks; draw 12-15 bold flat dark ovals; (3) FACE PLAIN AND PALE with NO supercilium and NO eye-stripe, and a pale surround to the eye giving an open, blank expression; (4) A PALE PATCH ON THE SIDE OF THE NECK behind the cheek; (5) UNDERWING LININGS WHITE, flashing in flight; (6) TAIL LONG with WHITE TIPS TO THE OUTER TAIL FEATHERS; (7) BILL dark with a pale base; LEGS PALE STRAW-PINK; (8) BODY LARGE, LONG-WINGED, and UPRIGHT, standing tall and bold - the biggest thrush in the set. ANTI-DRIFT: NOT a Song Thrush (which is smaller, warmer brown, with small arrowhead spots in neat rows and buff flanks), NOT a Fieldfare (no grey head, no chestnut back). If the spots are small or arranged in tidy rows, the output is WRONG.
